51007ffa0153c262: KUALA LUMPUR: Celebrity preacher and actor Muhammad Haris Mohd Ismail, widely known as PU Riz, is taking legal action against a Threads user over alleged defamatory social media posts.
According to Harian Metro, the controversy began when an event scheduled for Oct 24 involving Haris, 31, and his wife, celebrity entrepreneur Neelofa, 37, was cancelled.
Online backlash quickly followed over claims that the couple were offering non-cash options for ticket refunds.
​Speaking at a press conference at his office, Haris's lawyer, Faizal Rahman, explained that the Threads user had manipulated the refund issue to stir up anger.
The post quickly went viral, racking up over 9.2 million views.

​Faizal added that the individual had also shared screenshots of unrelated past issues solely to brand his client a "penunggang agama" (religious exploiter) and accuse him of teaching without valid credentials.

​Emphasising the gravity of the accusations, Faizal noted that labelling someone a "penunggang agama" carries serious consequences, particularly when targeted at a legitimate, credentialed religious teacher.
​As a result, a Letter of Demand was served via email and WhatsApp on Thursday afternoon.

The account owner was given 48 hours to meet five key demands: ​Delete the defamatory post. ​Issue an open public apology. ​Stop posting about Haris on any platform. ​Provide a written guarantee not to make future references. ​Pay RM1 million in compensation for damage to his reputation.
​Faizal warned that if the user fails to comply within the 48-hour deadline, full defamation proceedings will be launched in court.
As of Friday morning, the post remained online with no response from the account holder.

4f0b0909eea6afb5: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court in Shah Alam has ordered a contractor to pay RM15.32 million in liquidated damages to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for failing to complete works under the National Digital Network (Jendela) project in Sabah within the agreed timeframe.
The court also ordered MajuBina Resources Sdn Bhd to pay RM5,000 in costs to MCMC.
In a statement today, MCMC said the court had granted a summary judgment in its favour for RM15,324,832.31.
MCMC filed the lawsuit in February to recover liquidated damages arising from delays in carrying out works under Jendela Phase 1, which is part of the Universal Service Provision (USP) initiative.
The initiative aims to expand the coverage and accessibility of communications services, particularly in rural and underserved areas.
MCMC said all communications infrastructure projects funded through the USP fund must comply with contractual obligations and agreed timelines.

"Compliance with these requirements is essential to ensure projects are implemented smoothly and that the benefits of digital connectivity reach the public, particularly those in rural and underserved areas," it said.
The commission said the court's decision underscored the importance of accountability in implementing the country's communications infrastructure projects.
It added that it would continue to ensure USP funds were used responsibly to improve public access to quality communications services.

In December 2024, Bernama reported that Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor had been informed by MCMC that only 217 of the 382 Jendela Phase 1 towers in Sabah, or 57 per cent, had been completed.

In a separate report that month, Bernama quoted Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching as saying that a Non-Compliance Notice had been issued on Oct 28, 2024, to all Phase 1 and Phase 2 Designated Universal Service Providers that had yet to complete their Jendela projects.
She had also warned that contractors who failed to meet the deadlines could face measures including liquidated damages.
12b0a3da8c04cb8d: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with halal certification standards were seized during a midnight raid on a Puchong warehouse yesterday.
Twelve Bangladeshi and Pakistani men, believed to be involved in slaughtering and processing poultry at the premises, were also detained during the operation, codenamed Op Taring Chiller.

Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department Wildlife Crime Control Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid, conducted at 12.40am, uncovered premises suspected of being used to slaughter, process, and distribute fresh chicken without valid halal certification.
He said preliminary inspections revealed slaughtering and handling practices that raised serious concerns over compliance with Islamic requirements and the halal status of the products.
"Inspections found that the chickens were believed to have been immersed in hot water until they died before being slaughtered," he said in a statement today.

The integrated operation was carried out in collaboration with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department, Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim), Department of Environment, and Petaling District Health Office.
Zaki said authorities seized 468 plastic packages containing raw chicken weighing approximately 6,555kg, with an estimated value of RM85,400.

Preliminary investigations indicated that the premises had allegedly been operating as a chicken slaughtering, processing, and distribution centre for some time, with supplies sourced from several poultry farms around Sepang.
"The processed chicken was believed to have been distributed to customers, including restaurants, grocery shops and supermarkets across the Klang Valley," he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 3(1)(a) and 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011 and Section 38(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
The 12 foreigners are also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.

4e66fee44c3ee6f3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The High Court today sentenced a couple to 30 years in prison after finding them guilty of trafficking 173kg of methamphetamine four years ago.

Judge Nurulhuda Nur’aini Mohamad Nor handed down the sentence on Adam Tan Seng Tek, 34, and Vietnamese national Nguyen Thi Kim Thanh, 33, after finding that the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt at the close of the defence case.
“The court finds that the prosecution has successfully proven its case beyond reasonable doubt and finds both accused guilty and convicted on the charge,” she said.
The court ordered the prison sentence to run from the couple’s arrest on Feb 24, 2022, with Tan also receiving 12 strokes of the cane.
According to the charge, they were accused of jointly trafficking 172,741.10g of methamphetamine at a condominium unit at Residensi Kiara Jalil 1 here at 9.30pm on February 24, 2022.

They were charged under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment and not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane, if not sentenced to death.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Goh Ai Rene sought a heavy sentence, citing the quantity of drugs involved at 172.74kg.

“In this case, I urge the court to take into account the weight of the drugs involved as well as public interest, apart from the fact that the second accused (Nguyen) is a foreign national who committed the offence in this country.
“Drug offences pose a threat to national security, public order and public health. Drugs were also declared the country’s number one enemy in 1983,” she said.

Lawyer Kee Wei Loon, representing both accused, sought life imprisonment for his clients, citing the sentencing trend in such cases where courts no longer impose the death penalty and instead opt for life imprisonment. — Bernama
cb6f283a17746d36: KUALA LUMPUR: The confidence and supply agreement (CSA) between the government and seven opposition MPs does not specify that the elected representatives will receive their constituency development allocations, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
However, he said, the funds would be disbursed to those who signed the CSA once the 2027 budget is approved in Parliament.
“No terms were stipulated for the MPs,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at a mosque in Bandar Tasik Selatan.
Anwar also dismissed suggestions by analysts that the CSA served as a reminder to components in the unity government against retracting support for his administration, calling it a “political view”.
“Such assumptions cannot be prevented. But I am here to say that there is nothing unusual about this (CSA).”
Yesterday, the government signed the CSA with six Bersatu MPs and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, who underlined two key reforms Putrajaya must undertake in exchange for their supporty.
The MPs want the government to limit the prime minister’s tenure, and separate the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor before the end of its term.
They also want to be allocated the same amount of constituency development funds that government backbenchers currently receive.
In return, the seven opposition MPs will support Anwar’s administration until the end of the parliamentary term, as well as the 2027 budget.
Commenting further, Anwar said such agreements were also made in other democracies, while he, as the then opposition leader, signed a CSA with Ismail Sabri Yaakob’s government in 2021.
He said the agreement reached yesterday was a positive development.

f13a1b1d8339ba39: SEPANG: Former moto3 rider Zulfahmi Khairuddin has stressed the need for Sepang Circuit to be resurfaced.
Zulfahmi said deteriorating track conditions at Sepang have affected grip levels across all three tiers of the world championships - Moto3, Moto2 as well as MotoGP.
"I can say that the track has gotten worse in terms of grip. A lot of the asphalt has come loose," he said during a media scrum at the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia on Friday.
"A lot of riders have complained that there is no grip. It is not just Moto3 riders who are complaining, even MotoGP guys are saying the same.
"If you look at the lap times, they are more than one second slower than the lap records here.
"That shows that the track conditions are not good. I believe this track has to be resurfaced because a lot of the corners are not in a good condition anymore."
Zulfahmi said the lack of grip has amplified the importance of finding the right set up for Moto3 rookie Hakim Danish Ramli ahead of the race on Sunday.
Zulfahmi has been mentoring and managing Danish since 2020.
"Bike set up is the most important thing for Danish. He needs to focus on his race pace," he said.
"We will be doing our long runs tomorrow (Saturday) morning but the conditions will not be exactly the same as the race is scheduled for 12pm on Sunday.
"At the moment, he is enjoying every moment here and we hope he will be able to deliver on Sunday."
Danish did well to place fourth in the afternoon practice on Friday, which saw him book his spot in the qualifying two group - which is for the 14 fastest riders - for Saturday.
cf1a3ae54be59752: SINGAPORE, Oct 30 — A 29-year-old Indonesian domestic helper has reportedly been sentenced to three years in jail for abusing a four-year-old autistic boy in her care, including punching him at least 23 times despite his attempts to protect himself.

According to Singapore’s CNA, the woman, whose identity cannot be disclosed to protect the victims, also kicked the boy’s head twice in a separate incident and recorded videos of her employer’s children naked.
The court reportedly heard that the boy was non-verbal and unable to alert his parents to the abuse, making him particularly vulnerable.

The woman, who began working for the family in January, also allegedly sprayed water directly into the face of the family’s one-year-old boy using a handheld shower head for 16 seconds, causing him to flinch and cry.
The abuse reportedly came to light in March when her employer discovered videos and photographs of the incidents, along with images of his naked children, on her phone.

Investigations subsequently uncovered four videos and two photographs showing the children naked in the toilet, with the woman having sent two videos and both photographs to her husband, CNA reported.
Prosecutors reportedly said the woman had acted out of exhaustion and frustration from caring for the autistic boy, but stressed that her circumstances did not justify the violence.

Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamed Riasudeen sought between 35 and 41 months’ imprisonment, while defence lawyer Ariffin Sha argued for a sentence of two years and 10-and-a-half months, noting that she had apologised and previously requested a transfer from the household.

Both sides reportedly agreed that the recordings of the naked children were not made for sexual gratification, although prosecutors argued that her position as their caregiver aggravated the offences.
In sentencing her, District Judge Sharmila Sripathy-Shanaz emphasised the serious breach of trust involved in abusing a child who could neither speak for himself nor seek help.

“Stress is not a license for violence nor is frustration an excuse for cruelty,” the judge said, adding that the sentence would have been considerably longer had there been evidence of physical injury.
6d77ebb2f9424433: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Home Ministry (KDN) has stressed that the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) Programme is not a pathway for refugees to remain in Malaysia permanently, obtain Permanent Resident (PR) status or acquire Malaysian citizenship.
KDN said any employment access granted to DPP holders is temporary and limited, and subject to conditions and government approval.

“DPP is also not an incentive or pull factor for new refugees to enter Malaysia. The government has set January 1, 2023 as the eligibility cut-off date, meaning only individuals who were already in Malaysia before that date may be considered for participation in the programme,” it said in a statement today.
KDN said possession of a card or letter issued by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) does not automatically confer eligibility.
It said the government will continue to repatriate refugees to their countries of origin and resettle them in third countries and that the implementation of the DPP does not change that objective.
“Instead, the DPP is a mechanism to identify, screen, document and monitor existing refugees while a final solution is implemented in accordance with the law,” it said.
KDN also clarified that granting employment access to DPP holders does not mean the country’s labour market is being opened up freely to refugees.

According to KDN, the implementation takes into account the actual needs of industries, particularly sectors that continue to face labour shortages for 3D (dirty, dangerous and difficult) jobs that are less likely to be taken up by local workers.
“Priority for employment opportunities for Malaysian citizens remains protected, in line with the foreign worker employment policy and national security interests,” it said.
At the same time, KDN said lawful employment access would enable refugees to acquire skills, experience and verifiable employment records.
“This can help them meet the criteria for alternative resettlement pathways to third countries, including employment mobility programmes offered by host countries,” it said.

KDN explained that the approach would also enable the government to manage foreign workers who are already in Malaysia in a controlled manner, thereby reducing the need to bring in new foreign workers to fill certain vacancies.
It said the refugee issue was a legacy problem that had persisted for decades and posed major challenges to the country in terms of the economy, society, security and law enforcement.
Therefore, KDN, together with the Foreign Ministry, will continue efforts to cooperate with countries of origin and third countries to facilitate long-term solutions. — Bernama
31829894ce209dd9: PENAMPANG: Three schools in Penampang will benefit from road upgrades in Buayan and Terian, with both projects progressing ahead of schedule, said Datuk Ewon Benedick.
The Penampang member of parliament said the improved roads would benefit SK Terian, SK Buayan and SK Longkogungan, located about 12km away, as well as about 3,000 residents in four villages.
"There are two schools in this area, namely SK Terian and SK Buayan.
"Another school is located about 12km from here, namely SK Longkogungan. This means three schools will benefit from these road facilities," he said during a work visit.
Ewon said some villagers, teachers and students currently have to travel on foot because of poor road access.
The upgraded roads are also expected to support agricultural and tourism activities in Kampung Terian, Kampung Tiku, Kampung Buayan and Kampung Longkogungan.
A previous NST report highlighted how volunteers had to hike through dense forests to deliver aid to villages in the area.
The RM73.868 million Buayan road upgrade project is 76.64 per cent complete and is 45 days ahead of schedule, with completion expected in August 2027.
The RM99.395 million Terian road upgrade project is 57.83 per cent complete and is 58 days ahead of its revised schedule after being granted an extension of time until May 2028.

Ewon, who is also Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III and Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, thanked the Federal Government, Finance Ministry and Rural and Regional Development Ministry for funding and implementing the projects.
258408f995623b77: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Dalam Negeri (KDN) menegaskan program Dokumen Pendaftaran Pelarian (DPP) bukan laluan untuk pelarian menetap secara kekal.
Katanya lagi, DPP juga bukan laluan untuk pelarian memperoleh status penduduk tetap atau mendapatkan kewarganegaraan.
"DPP merupakan mekanisme untuk mengenal pasti, menyaring, mendokumentasikan dan memantau pelarian sedia ada sementara penyelesaian akhir dilaksanakan mengikut undang-undang," menurut kenyataan.

Katanya, melalui DPP yang dilaksanakan pada 1 Jan lalu, kerajaan mengambil alih fungsi pendaftaran dan penentuan status pelarian yang sebelum ini dilaksanakan secara unilateral oleh Pesuruhjaya Tinggi Pertubuhan Bangsa-bangsa Bersatu bagi Pelarian (UNHCR).
"Program ini membolehkan pengesahan identiti, pendaftaran biometrik, saringan keselamatan serta pemantauan keberadaan pelarian dilaksanakan secara langsung oleh pihak berkuasa Malaysia," katanya.

Katanya, ketika KDN dan Kementerian Luar Negeri mengusahakan penghantaran pulang pelarian dengan negara asal atau penempatan semula pelarian dengan negara ketiga, DPP berperanan memastikan pelarian sedia ada dapat dikenal pasti, dipantau dan dikawal.
"Matlamat kerajaan adalah untuk mengurus keberadaan mereka secara teratur dan terkawal sementara usaha penghantaran pulang atau penempatan semula diteruskan," katanya.
Sementara itu, hanya individu yang berada di Malaysia sebelum 1 Jan 2023 boleh dipertimbangkan untuk menyertai DPP.
"Mereka yang memasuki negara selepas tarikh berkenaan tidak layak dipertimbangkan di bawah DPP. Pemilikan kad atau surat UNHCR juga tidak memberikan kelayakan secara automatik," katanya.
Pada masa sama, kad DPP merupakan suatu bentuk pas khas yang bersifat bertempoh, tertakluk kepada syarat dan boleh dibatalkan atau ditarik balik mengikut undang-undang.
"Sebarang akses pekerjaan yang diberikan kepada pemegang DPP adalah bersifat sementara, terhad dan tertakluk kepada syarat serta kelulusan kerajaan," katanya.
Berhubung akses pekerjaan bersyarat, kebenaran hanya diberikan kepada individu yang memenuhi kriteria ditetapkan, tertakluk kepada kelulusan kerajaan, serta terhad kepada sektor dan jenis pekerjaan.

"Pelaksanaan ini mengambil kira keperluan sebenar industri, khususnya sektor yang masih berdepan kekurangan tenaga kerja bagi pekerjaan bercirikan 3D (kotor, berbahaya dan sukar) yang kurang diceburi tenaga kerja tempatan," katanya.
Pada masa sama, akses pekerjaan secara sah membolehkan pelarian memperoleh kemahiran, pengalaman dan rekod pekerjaan yang boleh disahkan.
"Ini dapat membantu mereka memenuhi kriteria bagi laluan penempatan alternatif ke negara ketiga, termasuk program mobiliti pekerjaan yang ditawarkan oleh negara penerima," katanya.

Menurut KDN, pendekatan ini membolehkan kerajaan mengurus tenaga kerja asing yang telah berada di Malaysia secara terkawal, sekali gus mengurangkan keperluan membawa masuk pekerja asing baharu bagi mengisi kekosongan tertentu.
"Keutamaan peluang pekerjaan kepada warganegara Malaysia tetap terpelihara, selaras dengan dasar penggajian pekerja asing dan kepentingan keselamatan negara," katanya.
611d2f962d4c6233: PARIS: The French economy contracted in the third quarter, data showed Friday, and could be "headed for a wall" if the government is unable to get a deficit-reducing budget passed soon, the finance minister warned.

Gross domestic product shrank by 0.1% in the three months to September, the national statistics office Insee said, amid deepening concerns about the state of public finances and growing political tensions ahead of presidential elections next spring.
The decline came as inflation accelerated to 3.4% on an annualised basis in October from 3.1% in September, the fastest rate since January 2024, Insee said.
The French economy had already stagnated in the second quarter after contracting by 0.2% in the first.
"For three quarters now, there has been no growth," finance minister Roland Lescure told France Info radio.
"The conclusion to be drawn from all this is that, as of 2026, the French economy is at a standstill," he said.
"France is not heading toward a crisis. But if we fail to achieve the turnaround outlined in the budget, we are headed straight for a wall."
Insee calculated that production of goods and services fell by 0.1% from July to September, while household consumption expanded by 0.4%.
Investment contracted by 0.6%, and foreign trade also made a negative contribution to growth, shaving 0.6 percentage points off GDP growth.

Analysts said the GDP data would indeed make it difficult for the government to reach its overall growth forecast of 0.5% for the current year or even the 0.4% anticipated by Insee and the Bank of France.
Worries about France's high debt and deficits have sent its government bond yields soaring in recent weeks.

An underwhelming 2027 budget plan last month fanned concerns that government spending would remain high ahead of next year's presidential elections, in which the far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, seen as a fiscal populist, stands a chance of winning, according to opinion polls.
France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, with nationwide demonstrations on Oct 17 degenerating into some of the country's worst rioting in years.
The Yellow Vest movement and student unions have called for a new day of protests on Saturday.
ca52aa334dc959df: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Cabinet today approved proposals to amend the existing Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA), particularly provisions seen as restricting students’ freedom of expression and association, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the Cabinet also agreed to develop a new law that would eventually replace the UUCA entirely within a reasonable timeframe.
“The Cabinet today approved a proposal by the Higher Education Ministry to undertake two measures concerning the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA).
“The first is to amend the existing Act, particularly sections viewed as restricting students’ freedom of expression and association.
“The second is to develop a new law that will eventually replace the UUCA entirely within a reasonable timeframe,” he said at his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Fahmi said the Cabinet had also agreed for the Higher Education Minister to table amendments to the existing UUCA in Parliament this December.
“The amendments will specifically address provisions that restrict students’ freedom.
“In December, God-willing, the Higher Education Minister will table amendments to the existing UUCA,” he said.
He said the proposed amendments were intended to immediately remove provisions that restrict students’ freedom.

However, Fahmi said drafting a new law to fully replace the existing Act would take more time, particularly as it would cover matters such as university registration, listing, management and other related aspects.
“This is because the Higher Education Ministry needs to consider several new aspects of university administration.
“We expect this to happen in 2027, although no specific year or timeline has been formally determined during the meeting. But we are looking at next year,” he added.
972179a0e515e2cb: SEPANG: Former MotoGP rider Hafizh Syahrin Abdullah has urged Hakim Danish Ramli to keep his emotions in check and aim for a top-five finish at the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia, with a podium considered a bonus.
Hafizh believes the youngster has shown encouraging pace at Sepang International Circuit, but must avoid letting the pressure to deliver in front of his home supporters affect his riding.

Danish, riding for AEON Credit-MT Helmets-MSi, backed up that assessment by finishing fifth in Friday morning's opening free practice with a time of 2 minutes 11.834 seconds, just 0.249sec behind Spain's Alvaro Carpe.
He improved to fourth in the afternoon's Practice session, clocking 2:11.573 to finish 0.146sec behind Spain's David Almansa and secure direct entry into Saturday's Q2 session.
"As a rider, my advice is to stay calm and not think too much about the pressure. He knows what he needs to do on the bike," said Hafizh.
"Last year, he was in the leading group but unfortunately suffered a technical issue and could not finish.
"This year, he has looked strong in practice, so I hope he can finish in the top five. A podium would, of course, be a bonus."
Hafizh, Malaysia's first MotoGP rider, competed for Monster Yamaha Tech3 in 2018 before continuing with the outfit as Red Bull KTM Tech3 in 2019.
He now races for JDT Racing Team in the Asia Road Racing Championship's ASB1000 class.
The experienced rider believes Danish's familiarity with Sepang could prove valuable as he contests his first home Grand Prix as a full-season Moto3 rider.
He credited the training opportunities provided through manager Zulfahmi Khairuddin and SIC with helping Danish understand where he can push and where caution is required.
"As far as I know, Zulfahmi has given him very good exposure through his training schedule, with SIC also supporting him," said Hafizh.
"He has an advantage in terms of mileage at his home track. He knows Sepang's characteristics, where he can attempt an overtake and which corners he cannot push beyond the limit."
Hafizh also understands how the home crowd can lift a rider, having experienced that motivation throughout his own Grand Prix career.
"I always looked forward to my home Grand Prix because the motivation felt doubled or tripled," he said.
"Even when I was struggling or lacked confidence in the bike, it automatically pushed me to give my best."
Danish will seek to convert his promising practice pace into a strong grid position on Saturday ahead of Sunday's race.
0a13546a0660cc8a: PETALING JAYA: Lawyers for Liberty (LFL) has urged Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar to secure the immediate release of three Myanmar children denied bail after being charged with criminal intimidation.
LFL adviser Latheefa Koya described the decision to deny bail to the children aged between 11 and 12 as disturbing, particularly as they came from a vulnerable refugee community.
Latheefa said the denial of bail was unlawful as the offence was bailable, and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) had itself proposed bail for the children.
“I think every decent person is shocked by this news. Remanding three children of such a young age without bail is extremely disturbing to Malaysians,” she told FMT.
“As the public guardian, the AG has the responsibility to intervene in this matter and ensure the immediate release of the children from being jailed.”

She also expressed hope that a High Court judge would intervene by ordering the case file to be brought up for revision and review of the magistrate's decision on their own initiative, known as suo motu.

Latheefa questioned how the children's welfare, education and other needs would be protected while in detention, warning that their detention could cause lasting psychological harm given their young age.
She said the proceedings also raised concerns about Malaysia's obligations under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, to which the country is a signatory.

Lawyer V Vemal Arasan also called for an urgent review, saying a High Court judge could request the case records from the magistrates' court and initiate a revision without waiting for an application.
He cited Sections 323 to 325 of the Criminal Procedure Code and Section 31 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 as the legal provisions for such intervention.
Vemal said the judge could call for the records on their own initiative and review the bail decision immediately.
The three children, two aged 11 and one aged 12, were today charged with criminally intimidating a 71-year-old woman in Taman Sri Rambai, Bukit Mertajam, on Oct 22.

They pleaded not guilty before magistrate Roshayati Radellah, who denied them bail and fixed Nov 10 for the submission of documents and the appointment of a Myanmar interpreter to read the charges to them again.
They were accused of threatening to hurt the woman using a mop, an iron rod, a fluorescent light tube and stones.
The charge under Section 506, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or both.
The children and their parents were seen sobbing in court after bail was denied, reported Harian Metro.
6756ea6ae11fc975: PUCHONG: Kelantan and Terengganu are expected to experience continuous heavy rain in November, followed by Pahang and Johor in December, and Sarawak in January, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said.

Its National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain were expected between November and January during the early phase of the northeast monsoon.
He was presenting the department's outlook at a media engagement session on the government's monsoon preparations at the Special Malaysia Search and Rescue Team (Smart) headquarters here.

Also present were National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim, Malaysian Civil Defence Force deputy chief commissioner (operations) Ghazali Abdul Rahman and Smart commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa.
The monsoon began on Oct 27 and is expected to last until mid-March.
Maqrun said warnings of continuous rain, strong winds and rough seas would be issued up to three days in advance.
The risk of major floods would increase if prolonged heavy rain coincided with high tides.

Despite the expected heavy-rain episodes, total monsoon rainfall is forecast to be below the climatological average, particularly in the northern peninsula, Perak, Sabah and parts of Pahang and Kelantan.
Maqrun also said El Niño had reached a strong level by September and was expected to exceed 2.0°C, reaching the "super" level, by the end of the year.
The phenomenon is expected to persist until mid-2027.
During the 2015/16 super El Niño, rainfall during the monsoon fell by 30 per cent in the peninsula and 45 per cent in Sabah, while Sarawak did not experience a significant decline.
Several states are also forecast to receive below-average rainfall in specific months.
These include southern Johor and eastern Sabah in October, and Sabah from November to March.
Perlis and Kedah are expected to receive less rainfall from January to March, while Penang and Perak are forecast to see a similar trend from February to March.
In March, Kelantan, Pahang, Labuan, Sabah and Sarawak are expected to receive slightly below-average rainfall.
Southern Sarawak, however, is expected to receive slightly above-average rainfall in January.
From January to March, rainfall is expected to decline further, particularly in the northern states and Sabah, bringing hotter and drier conditions with the potential for more extreme heatwaves.
e19d0b5376a49fb5: PUCHONG, Oct 30 — The public has been advised against panic buying or excessively stockpiling food amid concerns over the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), and instead to make preparations according to their respective needs.

Meor Ismail said the public should take basic precautionary measures, including keeping important documents and belongings in elevated places to prevent them from being damaged in the event of floods.

He also advised families with elderly members, persons with disabilities (PwD) and pregnant women to plan their evacuation to safer locations in advance if their residential areas are at risk of flooding.
He said the public should also stay informed of weather updates and forecasts from official sources and move to temporary relief centres immediately when instructed to do so.

73b7d9fbda970931: PUCHONG: The areas of the country that rarely experience floods are the biggest concern ahead of this year's Northeast Monsoon, despite forecasts indicating that flooding will be at its lowest level, says the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma).
Its director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said areas accustomed to flooding generally had better response mechanisms in place, while less frequently affected areas might be less prepared.
"Based on the forecast so far, we think this year's floods will be the lowest. We pray the forecast is right," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference during a media engagement session at the Special Malaysia Search and Rescue Team (Smart) headquarters here.

Also present were Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi, Malaysian Civil Defence Force (CDF) deputy chief commissioner (operations) Ghazali Abdul Rahman and Smart commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa.
According to Nadma's presentation, 101,901 personnel from five agencies are on standby, alongside 8,321 temporary evacuation centres (PPS) with a combined capacity of 1,907,145 people.
The number of flood hotspots has also declined to 3,045 this year, compared with 5,648 in 2023.
Nadma has set aside 60,000 food kits and 170,000 retort meals for distribution.
Meor Ismail, who has been involved in managing monsoon floods for almost five years, said his greatest concern was areas that rarely experienced flooding.
"What worries me most are areas that rarely flood.

"In areas that usually flood, when I visit, I see the responses are good, with the district office, health department officials, Fire and Rescue Department and Civil Defence all used to it. In new areas, I'm more worried," he said.
He stressed that a lower flood forecast did not mean preparations could be scaled back.
"I've issued the same instruction to the agencies," he said, adding that some might otherwise become complacent.
Meor Ismail said Nadma had not identified any new flood-prone areas for this season.
"We prepare all the usual areas. I have also instructed that even places that don't flood must be ready," he said.
'Move early'
He advised residents in flood-prone areas to evacuate early once MetMalaysia issued its three-day forecast.
"I'm not saying 100 per cent, but when MetMalaysia's three-day forecast comes out, it is very nearly right, so we hope people act," he said.
He said those with vehicles should evacuate on their own, while people with disabilities, young children and expectant mothers should be prioritised for early evacuation.
"When a rescue boat comes, each carries only about 10 people.
"If a housing area floods with 1,000 residents, how many boats would you need? That's why we say, if you get the information, move early," he said.
'Preparations in place'
Meor Ismail said Nadma had added permanent relief centres this year and introduced community-based disaster risk management programmes in several states.
Almost all state disaster command centres were also now in place.
He said assets such as boats had been positioned in areas where flooding was expected, while assistance could reach other locations within 24 hours.

Local leaders and village heads were often the first responders, he said, adding that the Fire and Rescue Department usually allowed fishermen's associations on the East Coast to assist in rescue operations.
Meor Ismail declined to disclose the locations of the 3,045 flood hotspots, citing potential implications.
"I don't want to be specific. Hotspots have other implications, and sometimes we can't state where they are.
"I'd rather not say, because there can be implications," he said.
He said residents were familiar with the hotspots as areas that regularly experienced flooding, and that the relevant agencies were aware of them and had made preparations.

5baff2e67cd0deb4: ‘Let us eat what we produce; that way, we all win’
Originally published on Global Voices
REB Lokal founder Rébetha Charles stands with a jar of peanut butter (manba lokal). Photo courtesy of Rébetha Charles, used with permission.

For several decades, due to the significant reduction of tariff barriers on foreign goods — particularly those from the United States and the Dominican Republic — Haiti has depended heavily on imported products for local consumption.

The arrangement began under various structural adjustment programmes that were initiated between 1994 and 1995, through agreements between the Haitian government and international financial institutions like the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. Since then, imports have practically invaded the Haitian market, creating inequitable competition for local farmers who rely on subsistence agriculture and traditional, rudimentary equipment, and significantly weakening national production.

Complicating the economic reality is Haiti’s ongoing struggle with gang violence, political instability, and the absence of adequate infrastructure; yet, many Haitians continue to take on ambitious initiatives. Take Rébetha Charles, a 38-year-old woman entrepreneur. Originally from Jérémie, Charles studied agronomy, works in the Grand’Anse department in Haiti’s southern region, of which Jérémie is the capital, and created an agri-food enterprise called REB Lokal.
Rébetha Charles. Photo courtesy of Rébetha Charles, used with permission.

REB is a short form of her name; Lokal speaks to the pride inherent in making local products. Her company buys products from small farmers and, in its small manufacturing plant, transforms these local harvests into healthy, sustainable, tasty products.

In a WhatsApp interview, Charles says she is proud of a few key things. First, her company adds value. Through a manufacturing process that produces authentic, nutritious, and 100 percent local products, farmers have a much better guarantee of not losing their crops, whereas before, various obstacles, including spoilage, prevented them from selling their produce at market.

Charles explains that the REB Lokal project is an enterprise that transforms local agricultural products: “We work with a supplier network of almost 2,000 people, including agricultural producers and small traders. We have more than 20 employees, so we work every day to grow the project even more.”

Second, Charles is pleased with the company’s focus on providing safe, fresh food that meets modern food processing standards — its approach places value on Haitian culinary traditions to preserve the natural taste and nutritional value of local ingredients. Finally, REB Lokal makes a point of avoiding chemical additives and artificial ingredients, as part of its commitment to providing consumers with healthy, accessible, community-friendly food.

Charles didn’t initially see herself as an entrepreneur. Before she decided to enter the agro business, she was working at an international humanitarian organisation, but resigned because of a culture — fairly common in Haiti — of sexual harassment. “In Haiti,” she stresses, “a woman’s life is not easy when it comes to work. Instead of competence, sometimes there are other things they ask from us. Sometimes, some of us stand up and say, ‘No, we do not agree,’ because we went to school just like everyone else, got experience where we needed — and after that, there are things we choose not to do.”

That professional environment left her with “such a disgust for work” that, even though she had been offered other opportunities in bigger organisations, she decided to put everything on pause. Charles finally submitted her resignation letter on August 31, 2020, and launched the REB Lokal project the very next day.
Workers packaging chocolate balls at the factory. Photo courtesy of Rébetha Charles, used with permission.

It wasn’t easy for Charles, especially at the beginning. In an interview with Chef Cassy, she said she started the business doing papita — breadfruit and banana chips — but spent more than five months making it, every single day, without getting it right. It was only by the sixth month that the papita started coming out well, and she began selling it in supermarkets. After that, things started moving quickly; every day, customers would place more orders — not bad for a small business that began with about USD 8.50, selling papita.

The business has now evolved to the point where it offers a broad range of widely available products: “We sell [our products] in the Grand’Anse department, we sell them in the south, in the west, in several other departments in the country, and we also sell internationally in the United States and Canada.”
Everything has grown out of her core commitment to Haitian farmers by purchasing their crops, and encouraging Haitian consumers to eat local products:

Mwen panse li lè li tan pou peyizan yo kapab vann sa yap pwodui. Donk, mwen santi m toujou gen yon responsabilite depi m pase yon kote ki gen dennre, bagay nou yo kap fèt nan andeyò yo, mwen anvi fè yon bagay. Ann manje sa nou pwodui, ann manje sa nou fè. Sa ap pèmèt peyizan yo pa bezwen deplase kite lakay yo pou yo ale lòt kote; yo ka rete nan zòn yo, yap travay, n ap achte, n ap kondisyonnen, nap transfòme, ou menm wap konsome. Konsa, nou tout ap soti gayan, e nap gen yon lòt peyi, nap gen yon lòt kominite.

I think it is time for farmers to be able to sell what they produce. So, I always feel a responsibility whenever I pass by a place that has crops, or things made in the countryside; I want to do something. Let us eat what we produce, let us eat what we make. This will allow farmers to not need to leave their home to go somewhere else; they can stay in their area — they work, we buy, we process, we transform, and you consume. That way, we all win, and we will have another country; another community.

Inside REB Lokal’s processing facility feels different from what one would expect. There are production rooms, transformation rooms, and packaging rooms where employees work in white coats, hairnets, and gloves.
Customers inside the REB Lokal store looking at products. Photo courtesy of Rébetha Charles, used with permission.

There is also a shop front full of shelves with finished products — now much more diverse than just papita — displayed for sale. There are roasted peanuts, sakalapina (cornmeal with avocados), papita in both chicken and fish flavour, konparet (spiced ginger-coconut cake), corn chanchanm (traditional Haitian sweet, made from roasted corn and peanuts), honey, sugar cane syrup, chocolate powder and balls, cocoa butter, breadfruit, corn, cassava and plantain flour, baby food (made without chemicals under the supervision of paediatricians and nutritionists), alcoholic drinks, fruit juice, and castor oil.

To Rébetha Charles, who grew up in an idyllic rural community, the work of REB Lokal is close to her heart. Yet, running a business in an insecure country comes with its challenges. Gangs’ control of the main roads can make delivery slow and limit production, as the lack of access prevents products from reaching many communities. A true entrepreneur, Charles finds ways around such obstacles as best she can. She still believes that Haiti has a future, so she perseveres, believing the impossible can become possible through vision and sheer willpower.
Written by Jude Pierre Louis
576ec67c5c89523c: SINGAPORE, Oct 30 — Singapore has selected seven investigation and legal specialists to assess companies identified by its government as potentially linked to transboundary haze, as authorities move to strengthen enforcement against firms suspected of contributing to fires.

Singapore’s CNA reported today that the panel comprises investigation firms Control Risks Group, FTI Consulting (Singapore) and Kroll Singapore, alongside Dentons Rodyk & Davidson, Toby Landau KC of Duxton Hill Chambers, TSMP Law Corporation and WongPartnership.

Singapore’s Ministry of Law (MinLaw) and National Environment Agency (NEA) separately confirmed the appointments in a joint statement, saying the panel members have expertise spanning forensic investigations, financial analysis, corporate intelligence, risk advisory and legal services.

Companies identified by the government will reportedly be required to engage an NEA-selected team comprising an investigation firm and a law firm or legal adviser from the panel, with the assessment carried out at the companies’ own expense.
The assessors will examine their operations, corporate relationships and supply chains, before submitting findings to NEA for consideration in deciding whether further action is warranted.
Davinder Singh Chambers has meanwhile been appointed as the government’s adviser and will coordinate the panel’s work to ensure its reports provide the information and evidence required by NEA.
The Singapore government also plans to table amendments to the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014 at the next parliamentary sitting to give legal force to the assessment framework.

CNA said the move follows a meeting on Wednesday between senior executives representing 10 companies under scrutiny and Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, Senior Minister K Shanmugam and Sustainability and Environment Minister Grace Fu.
The companies pledged to cooperate with Singapore’s investigations, which could include giving assessors access to relevant documents, personnel and premises.
Wilmar International has become the first of the 10 to publicly say it will voluntarily engage, at its own cost, an investigation firm and law firm from the government panel, according to CNA.

61bf00d6cb864162: BENGALURU: AstraZeneca on Friday launched an unexpected restructuring drive aimed at investing in its new drug pipeline, hoping that annual savings of about US$1.5 billion from the plan will keep the drugmaker on track to achieve its long-term ambitions.

AstraZeneca has been stepping up investments across therapy areas as long-time CEO Pascal Soriot seeks to reassure investors that recent trial setbacks have not undermined the company's target of generating US$80 billion in annual revenue by 2030 from about 20 expected new drug launches.
AstraZeneca reported US$34.36 billion in operating expenses last year.
Still, the stock has fallen around 5% in 2026 as of Thursday.

"With multiple potential blockbuster assets in late-stage development and transformative technologies scaling rapidly, we are on track to deliver our 2030 ambition and to sustain growth through the next decade," Soriot said in a statement.

Drugmakers globally are facing rising scrutiny over their research and pipeline engines, with valuations increasingly dependent on delivering successful late-stage trial outcomes rather than on established blockbuster medicines that will lose patent protections.

Concerns over AstraZeneca's pipeline had intensified following setbacks for camizestrant and Wainua, though investors broadly have been confident that the drugmaker's scale and depth of late-stage assets leave it well positioned to weather individual drug failures.

A Citeline report in January showed AstraZeneca leading in new drug development programmes and with the most Phase III or late-stage trial assets among the 10 top drugmakers globally. The company has more than 180 projects in its pipeline, it said on Friday.
The restructuring plan was announced alongside third-quarter results, which surpassed analyst expectations for sales and profit and prompted the company to maintain its outlook for 2026.
British rival GSK in July also laid out a cost-savings plan to fund drug development and prepare for looming patent losses.

"Being Malaysian is just in your blood," Kelly said.

"I made six birdies, but I'm hungry for more. We just need to catch that momentum and get hot over the weekend."

For amateur star Mirabel Ting, the turnaround began with a late-night conversation with her coach and sister after a frustrating opening-round three-over 75 to tie for 46th with Australian Grace Kim, Japanese Chizzy Iwai and Hinako Shibuno, America's Jenny Bae, Dewi Weber of the Netherlands and Thailand's Suvichaya Vinjichaitham.
The 21-year-old said she had been struggling to identify what went wrong before seeking advice ahead of the second round.
"I was lost yesterday after the round, just so confused," Mirabel said.
"Before bed, I had late-night talks with my coach and my sister to figure out what was spinning through my head. It helped me wake up knowing what to focus on, the process, not just results."
The discussions paid off as Mirabel carded a four-under 68 to improve to one-under 143, seven shots better than her opening round.
Meanwhile, qualifier Liyana Durisic remained the leading Malaysian in the clubhouse at four-under 140 after following her opening 67 with a one-over 73.
But she dropped from her tied sixth spot on Thursday to tied 28th alongside South Korea's Kang Min Ji, Achhiraya Sriwong of Thailand and American Lindy Duncan.
Her round began with an unexpected change as her brother and regular caddie Danial Aizat had to attend to an emergency, leaving an unnamed friend to take over the bag at short notice.
Despite an early bogey and a double-bogey on the par-four 14th after an unfortunate flyer lie, Liyana kept her composure.
"I told myself: 'Tough luck, walk away with a double. Five holes left is still a lot of golf,'" she said.
"My friend on the bag was great — we didn't talk about golf at all, which was the exact distraction I needed.
"There are still 36 holes to play. I'm capable of going low, and the next two days will show it."

53362ec38d8502b0: KUALA LUMPUR: Big Tree, Malaysia's leading out-of-home (OOH) advertising solutions provider, has demonstrated how interactive advertising can go beyond traditional media planning through its Big Tree OOH City Tour 2026.

The initiative, held under the theme 'What If the City Could Hear You?' and the tagline 'Don't Just Plan OOH. Become Part of It.', placed advertising agency professionals at the centre of an immersive urban experience.
It aimed to show how OOH advertising can move beyond conventional media placements through digital creativity and audience participation.
Big Tree, a subsidiary of Media Prima, transformed selected locations across Kuala Lumpur into interactive showcases. Participants experienced its digital out-of-home (DOOH) network first-hand.

The tour began at Big Tree's Cosmic Towers, a dual-screen DOOH installation with sound at the entrance to NU Sentral. Participants were welcomed through a personalised sequence featuring their faces on giant digital screens.
The activation demonstrated how digital advertising installations in high-traffic urban areas can create personalised experiences for audiences.
Participants then travelled by LRT to explore Big Tree's DOOH network across transit environments before visiting pedestrian connections around KLCC.
These locations highlighted how OOH advertising can reach audiences as they move between transport hubs, shopping destinations and workplaces.
The experience continued aboard a double-decker bus, which took participants past several of Big Tree's prominent DOOH installations across the city.

During the journey, participants saw their faces displayed on digital screens along the route. This demonstrated how the medium can combine visibility across multiple locations with personalised audience engagement.
Participants were also invited to submit selfies accompanied by personal messages they wanted to share with the public.
The submissions were featured on CuBig at the KLCC Junction, which Big Tree describes as its largest DOOH screen in Malaysia.
Using artificial intelligence (AI), participants' selfies were brought to life through anamorphic effects on the screen, alongside their respective messages.
The finale brought the activation's central theme to life, allowing participants to see their own messages displayed on a prominent digital screen in the city.

By combining strategic locations, digital creativity and audience participation, Big Tree aimed to give agency professionals a broader understanding of how OOH advertising could be incorporated into campaigns.
The Big Tree OOH City Tour 2026 was organised in collaboration with Omnia, Media Prima's integrated solution provider.
The initiative also reflected Media Prima's continued commitment to industry engagement, media innovation and exploring opportunities in an evolving media landscape.
To learn more about Big Tree, visit its official website.
3c1d0800ee20da4b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Two men pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to charges of creating and posting extremely offensive comments against Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, on social media in August.

The accused, unemployed Abdullah Aidid Mochtar @ Ahmad Duta, 44, and graphic designer Ashadi Zul’izzi Zainal Abidin, 46, entered the plea after the charges were read before Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad.

Abdullah Aidid is accused of creating and initiating the transmission of extremely offensive communications with intent to offend through the TikTok account “rookiebenz_albenzauto” at 11.27pm on August 1, while Ashadi Zul’izzi is accused of the same act via the Threads account “razakahmad725” at 2.39pm on August 4.
The posts were viewed at Jalan Dutamas Seroja 5, Taman Segambut (SPPK) here at 12.34pm on August 4 and 12.15pm on August 5, respectively.
Both were charged under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and face punishment under Section 233(2) of the same Act.
If convicted, they face a maximum fine of RM500,000 or up to two years’ jail, or both, plus a further fine of RM5,000 for each day the offence persists after conviction.

Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) prosecuting officer Nazrul Nizam Mohd Zameri offered bail of RM15,000 with one surety for each accused, citing the nature of the charges involving extremely offensive communications against the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
Abdullah Aidid, who was unrepresented, appealed for lower bail on the grounds that he had lost his job following the case and has been unemployed for the past three months.
Ashadi Zul’izzi, also unrepresented, sought lower bail as the amount offered by the prosecution was beyond his means.
The court then allowed each accused bail of RM12,000 with one surety and fixed December 1 for mention. — Bernama
372945c4476e20ed: KUALA LUMPUR: Defending champion Miyu Yamashita took control of the Maybank Championship with a bogey-free round, opening a two-shot lead after 36 holes at Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club (KLGCC) on Friday.
The Japanese carded a six-under-par 66 to add to her opening 65, moving to 13-under 131.
While the hot weather tested the field, Yamashita maintained her composure with precise iron play and effective scoring on the par-fives.
"My distance control has been consistent and I've taken advantage of the par-fives," she said.
France's Pauline Roussin-Bouchard and Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez shared second place on 11-under 133, two shots behind the leader.
Roussin-Bouchard, who led day one, continued her remarkable run with a three-under 69 to follow her opening 64, remaining bogey-free after 36 holes.
The Frenchwoman revealed she had consumed eight bottles of water and electrolytes during the round without needing a single toilet break, a reflection of the punishing heat at Bukit Kiara.
"I don't know if I should say that on camera!" she laughed.
"I drank all day and didn't go to the loo once. That is how hot it is out here. You just sweat everything out."
Her second round was built on patience and recovery, particularly after encountering plugged bunker lies.
"Today was all about damage control," said Roussin-Bouchard, who planned an ice bath for her feet alongside her usual evening gym routine.
"You can't let every shot feel too precious, or you start trying not to lose instead of hunting birdies."
Joining her in second place was Lopez Ramirez, who produced a six-under 66 despite a double bogey.
The Spaniard, who drew on her experience playing at the Solheim Cup, said competing on the team event's big stage had strengthened her confidence.
"Playing at the Solheim Cup on that massive stage gave me the mindset that if I can do that, I can play anywhere," she said.
Lopez Ramirez also enjoyed the support of local spectators, despite having no family members in Malaysia.
"I don't have family out here, so having the local fans adopt me and cheer me on has made this so much fun," she said.

With Yamashita holding a two-shot advantage, the chasing pair will need another strong showing to put pressure on the defending champion when the tournament enters its third round on Saturday where a US$3million (RM12.3m) prize purse and the iconic Tiger trophy awaits.

5a90f85f7f6d7b06: PARIS: The 2027 edition of the Dakar Rally will be held in Morocco following a prologue and first stage in Portugal, organisers Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO) said on Friday, five days after announcing that the event would not be held in Saudi Arabia due to security concerns.

"The Algarve will host the prologue and the first special stage. Morocco, with the aim of exploring its territory in its entirety, from north to far south, will host 11 stages and a rest day in Agadir," ASO said in a statement.
The 49th edition of the Dakar Rally, initially scheduled to run from Jan 1 to Jan 15, will now take place from Jan 9 to Jan 23, subject to approval by the FIA's World Motor Sport Council.
"The relocated 49th edition of the Dakar will meet the sporting standards that have always made it the most demanding rally-raid event," Dakar director David Castera said.
"Despite the short timeframe we have had to work with, we have designed a true Dakar."
Dakar 2027 will feature a total distance of 7,824 km, including 4,341 km of special stages, from Loule-Faro to Marrakech.

ASO said on Sunday that the decision to move the race out of Saudi Arabia was "exceptional and one-off". The 50th edition of the Dakar Rally in 2028 would return to the kingdom, which has hosted the event since 2020.

Morocco hosting the race means the Dakar Rally will return to Africa for the first time since 2008. The event started in 1978 as a race from Paris and across the Sahara to the Senegalese capital Dakar in West Africa, and has long been regarded as the world's toughest motorsport challenge.
It was later staged in South America between 2009 and 2019 after leaving Africa for security reasons.

f32f66cf110f46e1: PUTRAJAYA: The door remains open for other opposition members of parliament to sign the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) with the Madani government, following its signing by 13 opposition MPs recently.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the agreement was not exclusive to the 13 MPs, adding that any other MP interested in signing it was welcome to come forward for discussions.
"The CSA is not limited to these 13 MPs alone. It remains open to any MP who wishes to come forward, engage in discussions and sign the agreement.
"So, the door for discussions remains open," he said at his weekly press conference here today.
Fahmi said the cabinet had discussed the signing of the agreement at its meeting today, describing it as a positive development for the country's political stability.
"It reflects a spirit of cooperation in pursuing several institutional reform initiatives."

The agreement, signed yesterday, involved six Bersatu MPs, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and six independent MPs who had previously declared their support for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

The six Bersatu MPs were Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin (Pagoh), Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Datuk Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).

The six independent MPs were Datuk Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (Tanjong Karang), Datuk Syed Abu Hussin Hafiz Syed Abdul Fasal (Bukit Gantang), Datuk Iskandar Dzulkarnain Abdul Khalid (Kuala Kangsar), Mohd Azizi Abu Naim (Gua Musang), Zahari Kechik (Jeli) and Datuk Dr Suhaili Abdul Rahman (Labuan).
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof signed the agreement on behalf of the government.

Under the CSA, the signatories agreed to support the government's 2027 Budget and proposed institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister's tenure to two terms and separating the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor.
In return, they would receive constituency development allocations on par with those given to government MPs.

db626cc6957859a1: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged parents to take greater responsibility for their children's upbringing, warning that inadequate supervision could leave them vulnerable to social problems, including drug addiction.
He said parents had an equally important role in addressing issues affecting children and young people, alongside government intervention.
Anwar said the cabinet had discussed several matters today, including mental health problems and addiction, which required effective intervention.
However, he stressed that government efforts must be matched by cooperation from parents and families.

"Sometimes, parents do not even know whether their children are reading books, coming home late, completing their homework or beginning to get involved with drugs," he told reporters after attending Friday prayers at Masjid Al Muqarabbin here.
Anwar said he often heard calls for the government to address social issues, but parents must also fulfil their responsibilities.
"Besides the calls I hear every day for the government to act, I want to take this opportunity to urge parents to take responsibility," he said.
He urged parents to pay closer attention to their children's discipline, education and daily activities.
Anwar said he was often reminded of schoolchildren when attending events involving young people.
He said he regularly advised them to observe their religious obligations, focus on their studies and nightly revision, and respect their parents and teachers.
However, he was concerned about their future if parents failed to provide proper guidance.
"Seeing these children, so innocent, loving and well-behaved, is very touching.
"But I worry about their circumstances and their future if parents simply leave them to their surroundings without supervising and educating them," he said.
Anwar stressed that parental care, affection and discipline were vital in helping children avoid harmful influences.
He said tackling social problems required active support from families and could not be left to the government alone.
de7d3c23da142349: SUNGAI BULOH: Hong Leong Yamaha Motor Sdn Bhd is steering clear of a price war with Chinese motorcycle manufacturers, choosing instead to strengthen its brand, products and customer services.
Its general manager for big bikes, John Lau, said the company would continue focusing on delivering value to customers rather than competing solely on price with Chinese motorcycle brands.
"We have been always focusing on ourselves. I think most important is what we want to do with our customers and how we want to benefit the market.

"That is most important because price is not something that we always go into as a war. We want to deliver good customer service, make sure our products are there," he told reporters at a press conference held in conjunction with the company's launch of a new era in its big bike business.
Lau said the company was also focusing on improving customers' riding experiences through activities and engagement programmes, including potential overseas riding events.
"These are the things that we go daily on to actually improve. So we do not look at the pricing point as such," he said.
Hong Leong Yamaha managing director Loh Heng Choy acknowledged the competitive landscape, saying competition was inevitable in any business.
He said the company remained focused on continuously improving its products and services while strengthening its brand and expanding its business.
Hong Leong Yamaha is a subsidiary of Bursa Malaysia-listed Hong Leong Industries Bhd and a joint venture with Japan's Yamaha Motor Co Ltd.
Hong Leong Industries recorded a net profit of RM574.11 million for the financial year ended June 30, 2026, supported by improved motorcycle sales, higher market demand and a better sales mix.

In its fourth-quarter financial results, the group cautioned that competition was likely to intensify with the influx of more Chinese motorcycles into Malaysia, although demand was expected to remain healthy.

Meanwhile, Lau said the company currently holds an estimated 20 per cent share of Malaysia's big bike market and aims to strengthen its position through its expanded operations and distribution network.
He said the company was targeting to double its big bike business over the medium term.
"We are looking at the midterm. We are targeting to double up the business. That is our objective," he said.
Hong Leong Yamaha's expansion comes amid growing demand for motorcycles with engine capacities of 250cc and above.
To capitalise on the growing demand, the company is revamping its big bike operations through a dedicated completely built-up (CBU) initiative.
According to the company, total industry volume for the segment surged 73 per cent between 2025 and 2026, with medium-term projections pointing to an overall market volume of 110,000 units.
Under the strategy, the company plans to expand its existing line-up from seven models to more than 20 CBU and completely knocked-down offerings in the coming years.

The expansion is supported by a tripartite agreement between Hong Leong Yamaha, Yamaha Motor and DRB-HICOM Auto Solutions Sdn Bhd, combining manufacturing, distribution and assembly expertise to support the company's long-term growth.

38000787f28531ae: SEOUL, Oct 30 — South Korean actor Choi Bool-am, 87 widely known as the nation’s father figure for his portrayals of paternal characters in popular television dramas, has died, his family said Friday, Yonhap News Agency reported.
Choi, whose real name was Choi Young-han, died at around 10pm Thursday while receiving treatment at a hospital in western Seoul, according to his family.

The actor had experienced difficulties walking after undergoing surgery for a herniated disc in March last year, prompting him to step down as host of the KBS documentary programme Korean Food Table, which he had hosted for 14 years since 2011.
Choi became a household name through his role as detective Park Young-han in MBC’s long-running crime drama Chief Inspector, which aired from 1971 to 1989.
In an essay, Choi called Chief Inspector one of his favourite works, saying his heart still beats when he hears the theme song for the TV series, saying he learned a lot about life through it.

He cemented his reputation as a Korean father figure through his role in MBC’s rural family drama Country Diaries, which ran for 22 years from 1980 to 2002, one of South Korea’s longest-running television series.
Throughout his acting career of nearly seven decades, Choi was a versatile actor, with his performances spanning across TV, films and theatrical plays.

He was not afraid to take on small roles even after he became a household name and was known for playing roles of older people from early in his career, including playing former President Rhee Syng-man in his 80s when the actor was actually in his 40s.
He often appeared as husband and wife with fellow actor Kim Hye-ja in hit shows including Country Diaries to Princess Hours (2006), most recently.

Choi last appeared in Chief Detective 1958 (2024), the prequel to the popular TV series Chief Inspector, alongside actor Lee Je-hoon, who plays the grandson of Choi, who follows his grandfather’s path to also become a police detective.
Choi briefly entered politics in 1992, serving as a proportional representation lawmaker in the 14th National Assembly from 1992 to 1996 under the Unification National Party.
The actor’s hallmark laugh and easygoing attitude were traits that made him a beloved figure across different generations.
Choi emceed several current affairs and educational programmes, and his laugh became a favourite for many actors and comedians to imitate.

Being one of the country’s most acclaimed veteran actors, Choi received numerous accolades, including the Baeksang Arts Awards for Best Actor in both TV and theatre, the Daejong Film Awards for Best Actor and national merits.
He was also the first civilian to be appointed as an honourary National Investigation Headquarters director.
In addition to his acting and political career, Choi was devoted to promoting the rights of children and youth.
In recognition of his efforts, his funeral will be hosted by the Chorogusan for Children foundation.
The actor is survived by his longtime wife Kim Min-ja, also an actor, and two children. — Bernama-Yonhap
4ab9aa8f73da2af7: LABUAN: Menteri Pertahanan Khaled Nordin hari ini menerima dua pesawat tempur ringan FA-50M pertama yang diperoleh Tentera Udara Diraja Malaysia (TUDM), sekali gus menandakan pencapaian penting dalam usaha memperkukuh keupayaan pertahanan udara negara.
Kedua-dua pesawat yang dibangunkan oleh Korea Aerospace Industries itu tiba di Pangkalan Udara TUDM Labuan selepas diterbangkan dari Sacheon, Korea Selatan.
Khaled berkata, majlis penyerahan rasmi pesawat itu dijadualkan berlangsung pada pertengahan November ini di Pangkalan Udara TUDM Kuantan, Pahang.
“Perolehan ini merupakan perkembangan penting dalam usaha meningkatkan keupayaan ketenteraan negara dan mempertahankan kedaulatan tanah air.
“Ini juga bagi menyokong pembangunan keupayaan jangka panjang TUDM menerusi Pelan Pembangunan Keupayaan 2055 (CAP55),” katanya kepada pemberita di Pangkalan Udara TUDM Labuan.

Beliau berkata, kerajaan turut meneliti kemungkinan memperoleh kumpulan kedua pesawat pejuang yang lebih moden dan canggih bagi meningkatkan keupayaan pertahanan udara negara, namun negara asal bagi perolehan itu masih belum dimuktamadkan.
“Sebanyak 18 pesawat FA-50M diperoleh di bawah program Pesawat Latihan Tempur dan Pesawat Tempur Ringan, susulan perancangan TUDM untuk menamatkan operasi pesawat Hawk pada 2028,” katanya.
Khaled berkata, TUDM dijangka menerima keseluruhan enam pesawat FA-50M menjelang April 2027, manakala baki pesawat akan diserahkan pada awal 2028.
Katanya, kementerian akan menentukan jumlah pesawat FA-50M yang akan ditempatkan di Labuan selepas pesawat Hawk ditamatkan perkhidmatannya.
FA-50M merupakan pesawat dua tempat duduk yang berupaya melaksanakan latihan penerbangan anak kapal selain menyokong pelbagai misi operasi yang mencabar.
Pesawat itu mampu mencapai kelajuan maksimum sehingga Mach 1.2, iaitu melebihi kelajuan bunyi, selain berupaya beroperasi pada altitud tinggi.
Bagi memastikan kelancaran operasi skuadron baharu itu, 57 anggota teras termasuk enam juruterbang, enam pegawai kejuruteraan dan 45 juruteknik telah melengkapkan latihan di Korea Selatan.
Semua enam juruterbang dalam kumpulan latihan pertama itu juga berjaya menamatkan program latihan penerbangan pada 21 Okt lepas.

75a39db08d261e4e: SEOUL: South Korea will file criminal complaints against students caught cheating on a national university entrance exam with smart glasses and toughen penalties for their use, a government official told AFP Friday.
Sales of smart glasses – which allow the wearer to shoot photos and videos and interact with an AI assistant, among other abilities – are growing worldwide.
But so is a backlash around the gadgets, including concerns over people being filmed without consent and their use by exam cheats.

South Korea's notoriously gruelling college entry exam, known as the "Suneung", is essential for admission to top universities and widely regarded as a gateway to economic security and even a good marriage.
"The ministry will seek criminal charges against students caught cheating with smart glasses" in the future, Lee Joon-hyuk, an education ministry official, told AFP.
Under authorities' plans, students caught cheating with smart glasses will not be able to retake their exams for three years, an extension from the current penalty of one year.
But the new rules are unlikely to apply to next month's college entrance tests, Lee said.

"With only about 20 days left until the exam, it would be realistically difficult to amend the law before then. However, we plan to push for the changes to take effect from next year's exam," he said.
It comes after three students were caught wearing or possessing smart glasses during institution-administered essay exams at universities in Seoul.

Their use is an emerging issue at schools worldwide. This summer, the prestigious National Taiwan University in Taipei reportedly disqualified an entrance exam candidate for cheating using AI smart glasses.

Seoul's education ministry's new measures to prevent cheating using smart glasses, announced Thursday, included assigning a "designated staff member" at each examination centre to identify suspicious eyewear.

With so much at stake, on the day of the Suneung, a 35-minute nationwide ban on flights is imposed during the English listening test, except in emergencies, while banks and public offices tell their workers to start an hour later to avoid traffic on the roads.
Enormous pressure placed on students in South Korea's ultra-competitive education system has been partly blamed for teenage depression and suicide rates that are among the highest in the world.
ab7bc7e95cddfd80: SHAH ALAM: Selangor recorded the highest participation under the Migrant Repatriation Programme 2.0 (PRM 2.0), with 83,787 undocumented immigrants participating and RM42.61 million collected as of Sept 30.

Selangor Immigration acting director Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin said the programme provides an opportunity for foreigners who have overstayed or breached pass conditions to return to their home countries voluntarily.
He said the Selangor Immigration Department provides PRM 2.0 services across four locations to facilitate applications, namely in Shah Alam, Port Klang, Kelana Jaya, and Kajang.
"As of Sept 30, a total of 83,787 foreigners participated in this programme in Selangor, the highest number in Malaysia.
"The total collection under the programme amounted to RM42,614,240," he said at a press conference here today.
Khusairi said of the total participants, 60,913 were adult men and 20,293 were adult women.
He said the programme also involved 1,375 boys and 1,206 girls.
"The total collection comprises RM40,926,500 in compounds and RM1,687,740 for Special Passes," he said.
PRM 2.0 provides an avenue for foreigners who committed specific immigration offences to arrange their voluntary return to their countries of origin.
Participants must produce valid travel documents and return tickets to complete the repatriation process.
