c122698827c7b7bd: KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman from China has failed in his bid to recover RM2.1 million allegedly lent to a former PKR Perak deputy chairman and his wife.
The High Court found that although the couple were unreliable witnesses, Gao Kun had failed to prove that they had requested or received the money.
Judicial commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus dismissed Gao's lawsuit against Datuk M.A. Tinagaran Arumugam and his wife, Datin Latha Jothi.

The judge said the couple had given contradictory evidence, with parts of their testimony found to be untrue. However, weaknesses in their defence could not make up for Gao's failure to establish his claim.
"Disbelief of a denial is not affirmative proof of the fact denied.
"However poorly the defendants gave their evidence, the burden of proving that they requested and received RM2.1 million remained on the plaintiff from first to last," he said.
Redzuan made the findings in his written grounds of judgment, published by the Judiciary Department yesterday.
The court also ordered Gao to pay RM25,000 in costs.
According to the judgment, Gao claimed that he had given the couple an interest-free friendly loan in three cash payments between February and March 2021.
The payments allegedly comprised RM100,000 on Feb 19, RM500,000 on Feb 21 and RM1.5 million on March 4.
The two families became acquainted through their daughters, who were close friends at Garden International School.
Gao claimed that Latha had sought financial assistance through R. Sivamalai, also known as Mala, who was the English tutor to both children.
The alleged requests were made after Tinagaran was arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in February 2021 and remanded for six days.
Three personal bank accounts belonging to the couple were frozen following the arrest.
Gao claimed that the couple needed financial assistance to pay their employees, meet bail-related expenses and settle other financial obligations.
However, the couple denied requesting or receiving any money from Gao.
The court rejected the couple's claims that they were not facing financial difficulties, saying their explanations contradicted letters issued by their former lawyers.
The judge also criticised Latha for denying that the families were close, despite photographs showing that they had met on several occasions.
Tinagaran, meanwhile, gave contradictory evidence about engaging lawyer Datuk Selva Mookiah in connection with the freezing of his bank accounts.
The judge described both defendants as unsatisfactory witnesses, based on their demeanour and the way they answered questions during the trial.
However, he said these findings did not establish that the couple had received the alleged loans.
The court found that Gao had failed to produce bank records, withdrawal documents, receipts or written acknowledgements proving that the money had been handed over to either defendant.
The judge said Gao's case relied heavily on WhatsApp messages involving Mala, who allegedly acted as an intermediary between the parties.
However, although Mala was listed as one of Gao's witnesses, she was never called to testify.
The judge said she was the only person who could have clarified whether the requests for money had genuinely come from Latha or whether Mala had made them herself.

The court also found that although the WhatsApp messages were admissible under Section 90A of the Evidence Act, they carried little evidential weight in proving that the couple had received the money.
Gao was represented by Alliff Benjamin Suhaimi and Phoebe Loi, while the couple were represented by Noorazmir Zakaria, Syasya Sahira Mat Zainal and Mohamad Nakhaie Ishak.

68844bc95657d179: SHAH ALAM: A karaoke centre, two factories, and five blocks of flats were raided by the Selangor Immigration Department in an operation that saw 242 foreigners detained last night.
The Op Mega integrated operation across Shah Alam, Subang Jaya, and Klang saw 321 individuals screened, with 242 held for various immigration offences.
Selangor Immigration acting director Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin said those detained comprised 180 men and 62 women aged between 25 and 50.
He said 35 foreigners were held at the entertainment outlet, while 120 others were detained at two factories involved in plastic packaging and courier services.
"At the first factory, 62 foreigners were detained from 93 individuals screened, while 58 were held from 68 individuals checked at the second factory.
"Screening across five flat blocks in Pandamaran that housed foreigners led to the arrest of 87 individuals out of 110 people checked," he said at a press conference here today.
Khusairi said among the offences identified were failing to produce valid identity documents, breaching pass conditions, and overstaying.
He said five Form 29 witness summonses were also issued to five Malaysians suspected of being employers to assist in investigations.
All detained foreigners were taken to the Semenyih Immigration Depot for further action.
The operation, which began at 10pm and ended early this morning, involved 130 personnel from four agencies.
They comprised 115 Immigration officers, seven Employees Provident Fund officers, as well as four officers each from the Labour Department and the Civil Defence Force.
8991372b63c5ccda: LABUAN, Oct 30 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin today received the first two FA-50M light combat aircraft acquired by the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), marking an important milestone in the country’s efforts to strengthen its air defence capabilities.
The two aircraft, developed by Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI), arrived today at RMAF Labuan base, after being flown from Sacheon, Republic of Korea.
“The official handover ceremony is scheduled to take place in mid-November at RMAF Kuantan Air Base,” he told reporters at RMAF Labuan base here today.
Khaled described the acquisition as a significant moment for the country in enhancing its military capabilities and safeguarding national sovereignty.
He said the acquisition also supported the RMAF’s long-term capability development under its Capability Development Plan 2055, commonly known as CAP55.

He said the government would also consider acquiring a second batch of more modern and advanced fighter aircraft to further strengthen the country’s air defence capabilities, although the country of origin for future procurement had yet to be determined.

“The 18 FA-50M aircraft were procured under Malaysia’s Fighter Lead-In Training and Light Combat Aircraft programme, following the planned decommissioning of the RMAF’s Hawk aircraft in 2028,” he said.
Khaled said RMAF was expected to receive a total of six FA-50M aircraft by April 2027, with the remaining units scheduled for delivery in early 2028.
He said the ministry would determine the number of FA-50M aircraft to be based in Labuan following the decommissioning of the Hawk aircraft.
The FA-50M is a two-seat aircraft capable of supporting crewed flight training as well as demanding operational missions.
It can reach speeds of up to Mach 1.2, enabling it to fly faster than the speed of sound and operate at high altitudes.
Meanwhile, 57 core personnel comprising six pilots, six engineering officers and 45 technicians have completed their training in the Republic of Korea to spearhead the new squadron.
All six pilots in the initial training group completed their flight training programme on Oct 21.
Mohamed Khaled said the aircraft would be operated by No. 15 Squadron, which already has more than 200 personnel, with preparations for its home base centred at the RMAF Kuantan Air Base. — Bernama
8229e659410592d8: SEPANG: Following his struggles in recent rounds, Moto3 rookie Hakim Danish Ramli was all smiles after notching strong performances on the opening day of the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia on Friday.

Danish clocked a solid two minutes and 11.57 seconds to place fourth (+0.146s) in the afternoon practice session and subsequently secure his place in Saturday's qualifying two (Q2) group, which is for the top-14 riders from Friday.
Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP's David Almansa topped the session on 2:11.42s with Red Bull KTM Tech3's Rico Salmela (+0.069s) and Honda Team Asia's Veda Pratama (+0.092s) rounding out the top three.
Danish, who was fifth (2:11.834s) in free practice one (FP1) earlier, said he was relieved to rediscover his form at his home GP.
"My feeling on the bike here has been better compared with the last two or three rounds where I had struggled. Today, I got my feeling back," said Danish during his post-practice media scrum.
"I was also really happy to see all my fans, family and team members who came out here to support me, it definitely adds to my motivation.
"I felt really good with the bike during both sessions but of course there is still room for improvement."
"I struggled for grip a bit during the high-speed corners so the team and I will have to review the data and look at how we can improve the bike set up."
Danish said he will look to fight for a front-row spot in qualifying on Saturday.
"Of course my goal is to get pole position and be on the front row, but if that is not possible, I will still keep working hard," said Danish.
"I also have to work on my race pace to ensure that I can be competitive on Sunday."
The Aeon Credit-MT Helmets-MSI rider notched impressive results earlier this season, finishing third at Mugello and winning his maiden grand prix at Brno, both in July.
It was the first time a Malaysian had won a Moto3 race since Khairul Idham Pawi in 2016.
Danish's form has, however, tapered after the summer break. He only managed two top-10 finishes since his victory at Brno, the last of which came at the Red Bull Ring, four rounds ago.
afa12e3b8442b9c9: FORT LAUDERDALE: Soaring prices for gas, medicine and other cost of living essentials are preoccupying Americans as they start to cast their ballots ahead of next week's midterm elections.
A whopping 84% of voters who have cast their ballots early listed the economy as their biggest concern this election cycle, according to a recent Pew Research Center survey.
Kyler Daugherty, a 43-year-old health care worker, summed up the sentiment as he filled up his gas tank in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
"It's ridiculous. I mean, everything's gone up, from food to transportation to gas prices," he told AFP.
Fuel costs have skyrocketed around the world since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February.
US gas prices rose 9.1% in September alone, according to official figures, a headache for residents in a state like Florida, where most people rely on cars to get around.
"It affects transportation, it affects goods, it affects everything," Matthew Moore, a 63-year-old attorney, said after he cast his ballot early.
"We transport a lot by truck. Air prices have gone up. My tickets home for Christmas have doubled since last year," he said.
Broken promises
US president Donald Trump won reelection in 2024 in part because of his campaign promise to lower prices, which had also increased during the term of his predecessor Joe Biden.
"I didn't believe that promise then and I probably won't continue to believe (it)," said Melissa Reer, a 49-year-old social worker worried by her car and home insurance costs.
"But I think there's a lot more changes have to happen before prices can go down," she said.

William Galston, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution think tank, said two of Trump's decisions this term have directly contributed to cost pressures: launching the war on Iran and slapping tariffs on trade partners.
"It's within the president's power to remove most of the tariffs that he's imposed. It's within the president's power to end the war that he began," Galston told AFP.
For some voters, however, it's too late.
"My vote was cast based upon my feelings about how they've handled the stewardship that the voters have given them," said Michael Childs, 62.
The White House for its part insists that Trump's policies are revitalising the US economy and making life more affordable for Americans.
Basic expenses
However, millions of households across the US find it harder than ever to make ends meet.
"The financial hardship is creeping up in America, particularly the middle class," said Symeria Hudson, the CEO of United Way Miami, a nonprofit fundraising organisation.

United Way's ALICE metric - which stands for an Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed person - measures working people whose income does not cover basic expenses, such as food, housing and health care.
Nearly 41% of the 132 million households in the US fall below the threshold.
"We continue to encourage those policymakers to really understand the data," Hudson told AFP.
Many US voters are running out of ways to cut spending.
"I'm literally cutting back on certain meds because I'm like, 'I can't afford them.' I don't know what to do next," Daugherty said.
f7e09342bd11e5d6: Google is paying a higher price for its bet on AI than even Alphabet's $51.4 billion in Q3 capital expenditures suggest.

The biz appears to have traded its high-performing search advertising business for the mediocre monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode, a misstep that contributed to investor concerns as Alphabet lost roughly $500 billion in market value despite management's attempts to reassure Wall Street.
Google's year-over-year search revenue growth slowed from 17 percent in Q2 to 12 percent in Q3. It's still headed in the right direction, but at a slower rate.

During Alphabet's conference call for investors, Douglas Anmuth from JPMorgan Chase & Co asked whether that's because Google is showing fewer ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode than it shows in its traditional search results.

Chief business officer Philipp Schindler cited several reasons for that: foreign exchange rates, Europe's elimination of its customs-duty exemption, and "the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode."
To compensate, Google said it is expanding the distribution of AI Overview ads and adding multiturn ads in the US for AI Mode queries.

But some Google Ads customers appear to be more concerned about quality than quantity. In a social media post, Max Anderson, CEO of OnlyFinder, complained that Google has responded to declining search volumes by attempting to manufacture revenue growth through "short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics," such as charging advertisers more for lower-quality clicks, including clicks on search terms they had not agreed to target.
Eric Seufert, an analyst with Mobile Dev Memo, dismissed the doomsayers in a blog post.

"It’s tempting to look at the successive deceleration in Search revenue growth from Q1 2026 as a response to pressure from other chatbots and to assume that Search query volume is migrating elsewhere," he wrote. "But the earnings release notes that the 'year-over-year Search query growth rate [was] the highest it has been in the last five years' in Q3, so it's clear that Search usage isn't declining."

So people are still searching, and the business is still growing, but less convincingly, thanks to the lower monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode. And Google's answer involves more ads in AI interactions.
Nate Elliott, principal analyst for AI at Emarketer, told The Register in an email that AI represents a double-edged sword for Google's ad business.

"On the one hand, Google owns the thing that people use AI for most: search," Elliott wrote. "Our surveys say that by far the top reason people use AI is to look for facts and information. Luckily for Google, people also tell us they haven't stopped using search engines – they've simply added AI as a new behavior on top of search. That means people spend more time than ever looking for information, and most of those people don't even think twice before doing their searches on Google. If Google figures out how to effectively monetize those users, that's great news for them."
But, said Elliott, people may find tools they like better than Google Search as they become accustomed to AI-based discovery.

"If ChatGPT or Claude or Muse is better at helping them find what they're looking for, people's search habits might change for the first time in a generation," he said. "That's potentially catastrophic for Google's ad business. The same is true if they maintain their market share but simply can't figure out how to make money from this new kind of discovery.

"The problem is, Google isn't giving us very much information about what the specific impact is of AI on their business right now, so everyone's reading into the tiny scraps of information they are releasing."
Elliott said it's remarkable that Google has managed to keep the largest and most mature digital ad business growing at a double-digit rate every quarter in recent years.
"But it appears that most folks disagree, and instead are concerned that the advertising business 'only' grew by 10 percent," he said. ®

58117e3807fe3d99: KUALA LUMPUR: Actress and entrepreneur Nur Fazura Sharifuddin has shared a heartfelt message for her daughter, Nur Fatima Aisya, who celebrated her sixth birthday earlier this month.

b2fc66dcd070d74e: BERLIN, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump's economic agenda has delivered robust growth and strong investment but failed to reduce the trade deficit, according to a study by the German Economic Institute IW seen by Reuters on Friday.
Trump's tax cuts, tariffs and drive to revive domestic manufacturing had produced mixed results.
Gross domestic product growth remained solid and AI-related investment was buoyant, but job creation lagged the prior administration and inflation remained above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.
The US goods trade deficit reached US$130 billion in August, exceeding its level two years earlier, despite sweeping import tariffs.
Trade patterns had shifted, however. The European Union's share of the deficit fell to 7% from 20% in August 2024. China's share of the trade deficit declined to 14% from 29%.
Efforts to bring manufacturing back have so far fallen short. Foreign direct investment inflows fell 8.2% to US$248 billion in 2025, 18% below the 2015–2024 average.
The US-Israeli war against Iran is increasing already high public debt and pushing up interest rates, with creditors questioning whether the US can sustain its outstanding debt of US$40 trillion.
2003709f90854cd4: PETALING JAYA: Usahawan hartanah Azlan Abdullah akan merayu keputusan Mahkamah Sesyen Kuala Terengganu yang menolak saman fitnahnya terhadap pemilik akaun Facebook 'Che Wan AlaKazam'.
Azlan sudah mengarahkan peguamnya memfailkan rayuan di Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Terengganu susulan keputusan Hakim Wan Nor Aklima Wan Salleh, semalam.
Mahkamah memutuskan Azlan gagal membuktikan tuntutannya berhubung lima kenyataan Facebook yang didakwanya berunsur fitnah.
Beliau turut diperintahkan membayar kos RM30,000 kepada defendan, Wan Hafizie Wan Mohamad.
Mahkamah turut menolak tuntutannya bagi ganti rugi am, teruk dan teladan, selain permohonan injunksi kekal, perintah memadam hantaran serta permohonan maaf.
Dalam kenyataan, Azlan berkata beliau percaya mempunyai asas kukuh untuk mencabar keputusan itu selepas kes berkenaan melalui proses perbicaraan selama hampir tiga tahun sejak difailkan pada 2022.
Saman itu difailkan susulan beberapa hantaran Facebook yang menurut Azlan melabelkannya sebagai penunggang agama, penipu dan individu yang tidak boleh dipercayai.
Beliau mendakwa, hantaran itu mencemarkan maruahnya serta menjejaskan kredibiliti dan perniagaan yang dibangunkannya selama bertahun-tahun.
“Langkah rayuan ini diambil bukan semata-mata demi kepentingan peribadi, sebaliknya bagi mempertahankan prinsip keadilan, memulihkan maruah, serta menjadi iktibar kepada masyarakat,” katanya.
9d8489c4ee321e9d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — More than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with Islamic slaughtering requirements and halal certification standards were seized during a raid on a warehouse in Puchong here shortly after midnight yesterday.
Twelve Bangladeshi and Pakistani men, believed to be involved in slaughtering and processing chickens at the premises, were also detained during the operation, codenamed Op Taring Chiller.

Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) Wildlife Crime Control Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid, conducted at 12.40am, uncovered premises suspected of being used to slaughter, process and distribute fresh chicken without valid halal certification.
He said preliminary inspections revealed slaughtering and handling practices that raised serious concerns over compliance with Islamic requirements and the halal status of the products.
“Inspections found that the chickens were believed to have been immersed in hot water until they died before being slaughtered,” he said in a statement today.

The integrated operation was carried out in collaboration with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department, Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim), Department of Environment and Petaling District Health Office.
Mohd Zaki said authorities seized 468 plastic packages containing raw chicken weighing approximately 6,555 kilogrammes, with an estimated value of RM85,400.

Preliminary investigations indicated that the premises had allegedly been operating as a chicken slaughtering, processing and distribution centre for some time, with supplies sourced from several poultry farms around Sepang.
“The processed chicken was believed to have been distributed to customers, including restaurants, grocery shops and supermarkets across the Klang Valley,” he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 3(1)(a) and 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011 and Section 38(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
The 12 foreign nationals are also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. — Bernama
da779a6fa3e54414: KUALA LUMPUR: Tiada syarat dikenakan terhadap Ahli Parlimen untuk menerima peruntukan menerusi Perjanjian Keyakinan dan Perbekalan (CSA), kata Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.
Beliau berkata, peruntukan itu boleh disalurkan segera sebaik Belanjawan 2027 diluluskan Parlimen, selaras persefahaman yang dicapai.
“Tak ada syarat kepada mana-mana Ahli Parlimen, tak ada syarat,” katanya kepada pemberita selepas menunaikan solat Jumaat di Masjid Al-Muqarrabin, Bandar Tasik Selatan.

Mengulas pandangan penganalisis politik, CSA boleh menjadi peringatan kepada komponen kerajaan supaya tidak menarik sokongan terhadap kerajaan atau belanjawan, Anwar berkata tafsiran sedemikian tidak boleh dinafikan.
“Ini tafsiran politik, tak boleh kita pertikai, memang akan berlaku. Tetapi saya nak beritahu ini bukan sesuatu yang janggal,” katanya.
Katanya, persefahaman seumpama itu turut diamalkan di negara demokrasi lain dan pernah dilaksanakan di Malaysia ketika beliau menjadi ketua pembangkang, semasa Ismail Sabri Yaakob perdana menteri.
Menurutnya, rundingan ketika itu membabitkan wakil Pakatan Harapan (PH) dan kerajaan terdiri daripada Bersatu, PAS, Umno serta Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS).
Anwar menyifatkan persetujuan dicapai semalam sebagai perkembangan baik dan berkata, pihak lain juga boleh menggunakan pendekatan sama seperti kerajaan terdahulu.
Semalam, kerajaan menandatangani CSA dengan enam Ahli Parlimen Bersatu diketuai Presiden, Muhyiddin Yassin, dan Ahli Parlimen Muar Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Tujuh Ahli Parlimen itu mahu kerajaan mengehadkan tempoh jawatan perdana menteri serta mengasingkan peranan peguam negara dan pendakwa raya sebelum penggal pentadbiran semasa berakhir.
Mereka juga mahu menerima jumlah peruntukan pembangunan kawasan yang sama seperti diberikan kepada Ahli Parlimen penyokong kerajaan ketika ini.
Sebagai balasan, tujuh Ahli Parlimen pembangkang itu akan menyokong pentadbiran Anwar sehingga tamat penggal Parlimen, termasuk Belanjawan 2027.
Perjanjian itu turut ditandatangani enam bekas Ahli Parlimen Bersatu yang dipecat parti pada 2024 selepas mengisytiharkan sokongan kepada kerajaan.
756b7e715f197fdc: SEREMBAN, Oct 30 — Adat Perpatih, a matrilineal customary law system practised predominantly in Negeri Sembilan, must be preserved and documented through digital technology, academic publications and heritage education to ensure the state’s cultural traditions are not lost over time.

Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said safeguarding the heritage was not solely the responsibility of customary institutions and museums, but required the involvement of communities, educational institutions and government agencies.

“Knowledge of the customs, oral histories and traditional practices must be documented for future generations and made more accessible through interactive exhibitions to help the public better understand this heritage.

“Adat Perpatih is more than a set of inherited customs. It embodies a philosophy of life that emphasises consensus, consultation, justice and shared responsibility,” he said when officiating Perpatih Fest 2026, themed Adat Dijaga, Warisan Terpelihara here today.
Ismail said customary leaders, educational institutions and government agencies had an important role in ensuring traditional knowledge and practices were passed down to future generations.

Meanwhile, the menteri besar said Adat Perpatih and the cultural traditions of other communities also had the potential to contribute to the state’s economy through traditional cuisine, performing arts, handicrafts and local history as tourism attractions.

In conjunction with Visit Negeri Sembilan Year 2026, the state government aims to strengthen cultural heritage as a tourism product that attracts visitors while creating economic opportunities for local entrepreneurs.

Ismail said this year’s Perpatih Fest also featured a delegation from Thailand interested in learning more about Adat Perpatih, providing an opportunity to introduce the tradition to a wider international audience.

The three-day Perpatih Fest, running from today until November 1, features demonstrations of traditional luak customs, traditional games, museum and ethnic exhibitions, heritage cuisine and cultural performances.

The festival also includes seminars, discussions and forums on customary institutions and the cultural history of the Malay Archipelago, alongside traditional costume competitions and creative activities aimed at bringing cultural heritage closer to younger generations. — Bernama
921826eda2c154a7: TOKYO: Elena Rybakina withdrew from the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo with a neck injury on Friday, a day after she secured the year-end world number one ranking.
The Moscow-born Kazakh was due to face Canada's Leylah Fernandez in the quarter-finals, but instead she came onto the court to address the crowd and sign autographs.
She said she would return for next month's WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
"I just wanted to say thank you so much for coming today, but unfortunately I won't be able to play," said the 27-year-old.
"I've been struggling for a couple of days with a little injury.
"It's difficult for me to come and play at 100% since there is also a very important tournament coming up," she said.
Rybakina clinched the year-end top ranking with a 6-2, 6-3 win over Yulia Putintseva in her opening match in Tokyo.
She became world number one for the first time last month in winning the US Open, replacing Aryna Sabalenka at the summit.
The achievement capped a year in which Rybakina also won the Australian Open in January and now has three Grand Slam titles.
She arrived in Tokyo after winning her fourth title of the season last week at the Ningbo Open in China, beating Fernandez in the final.
"Thank you so much for all the support throughout the year, especially here in Tokyo," she said.
"It's an amazing city. I really enjoy it every time I come, but unfortunately this time I won't be able to play.
"Thanks again and hope to see you all next year," she added.
bfa7c6c42ba31428: PETALING JAYA: The home ministry has maintained that the refugee registration document, or DPP, programme is not a pathway for refugees to permanently settle in Malaysia.
The ministry said the programme is to reliably monitor refugees while it continues seeking to repatriate and resettle them.
"The government's aim is to manage their whereabouts in an orderly and controlled manner while repatriation or resettlement efforts continue,” it said in a statement today.

The ministry also said the decision to allow DPP holders to work in Malaysia was not meant to attract refugees to Malaysia, reiterating that this was limited to refugees who entered Malaysia before Jan 1, 2023.

It said the DPP holders will be limited to certain jobs, particularly those deemed dirty, dangerous and difficult, while their employment will be temporary in nature and subject to the government's conditions and approval.
"Malaysians will continue to be prioritised for job opportunities, in line with the government's foreign worker employment policy and national security interests," it said.
The ministry defended the decision to allow refugees under DPP to work, saying it would improve their skills and credentials, boosting their resettlement chances.
This would also reduce the need for new migrant worker intakes to fill certain job vacancies, it said.

It also said it was collaborating with the foreign ministry to pursue cooperation with countries of origin and third countries to enable a long-term solution for refugee repatriation and resettlement.
"National security, the rule of law, and the interests of Malaysians will always be the government's priority," it said.
37590b48c53469a2: MANILA: One of the Philippines' most active volcanoes fired a dark column of ash thousands of metres into the sky Friday in a "moderately explosive eruption" that lasted nearly six minutes, the state seismology office said.

There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage in towns and cities surrounding Mount Mayon, but the country's volcano institute raised the alert level from 2 to 3 on its 0-5 scale and called for evacuations within 6km of the crater.
The 3,000-metre (nearly 10,000 feet) ash column gradually drifted southwest onto nearby population centres, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology said in a bulletin.

"Mayon is in a new phase of magmatic eruption, with increased chances of lava flows and hazardous PDCs (pyroclastic density currents)... affecting the upper to middle slopes of the volcano in the immediate days to weeks," it said.

It urged local officials to evacuate areas near the crater "due to the danger of PDCs, lava flows, rockfalls and other volcanic hazards", with planes also advised to avoid flying close to the mountain.

The 2,462-metre (8,000-foot) Mayon, rising in a near-perfect cone about 330km southeast of Manila, is one of three Philippine volcanoes that have shown elevated levels of activity this year, though no major eruptions occurred.
In June 2023, more than 12,000 people living on its lower slopes were moved to evacuation centres to protect them from ash and toxic gases spewing from its crater.
Earthquakes and volcanic activity are common in the Philippines due to its position on the Pacific "Ring of Fire", where tectonic plates collide.
The country's most powerful eruption in recent decades was Mount Pinatubo in 1991, which killed more than 800 people and produced an ash cloud that travelled thousands of kilometres.
84577b14e1d2171b: PUCHONG, Oct 30 — A total of 101,901 officers and personnel from various rescue agencies have been placed on standby, with more than 40,000 assets ready for deployment during the North-east Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to last until March next year.

National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) Operations Coordination Section principal assistant director Major Wazirudin Mahfot@Mahbott said the personnel comprise 47,100 members of the People’s Volunteer Corps (Rela), 21,477 police personnel, 15,145 firefighters, 12,927 civil defence personnel and 5,252 armed forces personnel.

“Our preparations involve coordination among various agencies to ensure efficient rescue operations, evacuations and disaster management in the event of floods or other disasters,” he said at a media engagement session on the government’s preparedness for the 2026/2027 MTL here today.
Wazirudin said the assets on standby include 2,024 four-wheel-drive vehicles, 1,177 other vehicles, 174 ambulances, 2,425 boats, 28 aircraft, 27 drones and 35,301 life jackets.

He said technical agencies, including the Public Works Department and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), have also made available support assets comprising 17 units of heavy machinery, 575 mobile pumps and 30 generator sets.
Wazirudin said DID had identified 3,045 flood hotspots nationwide, with Kelantan recording the highest number at 609, followed by Pahang (572), Terengganu (460) and Sabah (348).

He added that data from the Department of Mineral and Geoscience showed that 31 landslide hotspots had been identified nationwide, including at Gunung Jerai in Kedah, Tanjung Bungah in Penang, Kundasang in Sabah and Cameron Highlands in Pahang.

Wazirudin also said the government had designated 8,321 temporary relief centres nationwide, with a combined capacity of about 1.9 million people, as well as two permanent relief centres in Johor and Pahang that could accommodate a total of 1,600 people.
On food supplies, he said 60,000 food kits and 170,000 retort food packs had been allocated, of which 29,900 food kits and 94,510 retort food packs had been distributed to all states.
“The remaining 30,100 food kits and 75,490 retort food packs will be distributed according to the needs of each state,” he said. — Bernama
2f9450f09c9e1390: JAKARTA, Oct 30 — Air pollution from smoke emitted by months of wildfires across Indonesia caused an estimated 3,560 deaths in the vast Southeast Asian archipelago in September alone, according to a scientific study.
The same month, about 57.8 million people were inhaling unhealthy to hazardous air, said the report by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Helsinki-based think tank.
“Worsening air quality due to forest and land fires in Indonesia pushed the estimated death toll to 3,560 cases in September 2026, a twofold increase from the August estimate,” said a CREA statement.
The study estimated the number of deaths brought about by short-term exposure to PM2.5 pollution, which are deaths occurring within days of exposure.
Most occurred on Indonesia’s part of Borneo island as well as on Java and Sumatra islands and the country’s east.

The researchers also looked at non-fire pollution from urban and industrial emissions, and found it had caused a further 1,750 deaths in September for a total of 5,310 in the country of around 278 million people. — AFP
7bc70a10d7131b7b: PETALING JAYA: The High Court in Shah Alam has ordered a contractor to pay RM15.32 million in liquidated damages to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission for failing to complete works under the National Digital Network (Jendela) project in Sabah on time.
The court also ordered MajuBina Resources Sdn Bhd to pay RM5,000 in costs to MCMC.
In a statement today, MCMC said the court had granted a summary judgment in its favour for RM15,324,832.31.
MCMC filed the lawsuit in February 2026 to recover liquidated damages arising from delays in carrying out works under Jendela 1, which is part of the Universal Service Provision (USP) initiative.
The initiative aims to expand the coverage and accessibility of communications services, particularly in rural and underserved areas.
The commission said all communications infrastructure projects funded through the USP fund must comply with contractual obligations and agreed timelines.

"Compliance with these requirements is essential to ensure projects are implemented smoothly and that the benefits of digital connectivity reach the public, particularly those in rural and underserved areas," it said.
It said the court's decision underscored the importance of accountability in implementing the country's communications infrastructure projects.
MCMC also said it would continue to ensure USP funds were used responsibly to improve public access to quality communications services.
442e7ed5c0ea201f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Australian Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk has said that she considered quitting the sport after facing widespread online abuse over an incident in which she soiled herself but continued competing during a race in Beijing last month.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC ahead of her return to competition in Hamburg, Germany, today, the world record holder described the past several weeks as a “mentally and emotionally taxing period”, revealing that even her family had received threats.

Wietrzyk said she had withdrawn from social media and tried to isolate herself following the backlash, which began after images of her competing with faecal matter on her body circulated widely online.
“Yes, I did make the wrong decision but I don’t believe I should have received such backlash and such scrutiny online… At the end of the day I’m only human,” she told the BBC.
The controversy began during a Hyrox event in Beijing on September 12, when Wietrzyk suffered a sudden bout of diarrhoea, which she attributed to a bacterial infection caused by food poisoning.
Despite the incident, she continued racing and crossed the finish line first, drawing criticism over the potential hygiene risks to other participants using shared equipment.
She subsequently apologised, forfeited her victory and withdrew retrospectively from the race, while Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste acknowledged that organisers should have intervened.
The competition has since introduced rules allowing race directors to remove athletes whose vomit, urine or faeces pose contamination or welfare risks.
Reflecting on her decision to continue racing, Wietrzyk said her competitive instincts had taken over and that she had failed to consider how her actions might affect others.
She also expressed regret over her initial response on social media, where she had defended her performance in a now-deleted post.
Now preparing for her first competition since the incident, Wietrzyk said she was nervous about returning but remained determined to continue her sporting career.
“I don’t want it to become my identity,” she said, adding that she believed she still had much more to achieve in Hyrox.
7fbdc63ecc639d05: PETALING JAYA: Zetrix AI Bhd can heave a sigh of relief as its bond holders are not demanding immediate repayment of the outstanding amount under its RM2 billion sukuk programme following a covenant breach.

However, the embattled digital services company confirmed a "dissolution event" was triggered following its breach of the covenant requiring its founder and managing director Wong Thean Soon to remain its largest shareholder.
Forced share sales triggered by margin calls on Wong’s share-backed financing facilities has slashed his stake to about 1.84% from nearly 30% prior to the sell-off which started end-August.

In a response to Bursa Malaysia’s queries, Zetrix clarified it is not required to immediately repay the full outstanding amount under its sukuk (Islamic bond) programme, and that no payment default had occurred.

“The company has made all payments due under the sukuk programme in accordance with the stipulated payment schedule,” it said in a filing yesterday. Its next payment is for RM214 million in March 2027.

Zetrix, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, acknowledged that a payment default could arise if it failed to repay the full outstanding amount when it became due and payable. It added that it would “make an immediate announcement if a payment default occurred”.
It also said that as no resolution was passed at the recent sukuk holders' meeting, the existing terms and conditions of the sukuk programme remain in force.
The company will continue to engage with the sukuk trustee and sukuk holders to address the outstanding matters, it added.
Zetrix’s woes were compounded when its wholly owned unit MyEG Sdn Bhd was slapped with a RM353.13 million tax bill from the Inland Revenue Board for the years of assessment 2021 to 2023.

In a separate filing yesterday, it said the assessment received on Wednesday comprises RM333.11 million in additional income tax relating to transfer pricing and RM20.02 million in deemed interest, including penalties.

It noted the government had filed a civil suit against MyEG over the matter. This comes on the heels of the government’s plan to take legal action over Zetrix’s failure to remit RM314 million in revenue collected on behalf of the Road Transport Department.
The company is also facing a leadership crisis after four out of seven board members, and all three of its audit committee members, tendered their resignation in recent weeks.
Othman Semail and Mohaini Mohd Yusof resigned as independent directors and members of the audit committee effective yesterday, according to filings with Bursa.
Their resignations come three days after Wong Kok Chau resigned as independent director and chairman of the audit committee.
The three remaining directors are Wong, 55, non-independent director Mohd Jimmy Wong Abdullah, 64, and Dr Norraesah Mohamad, 78.
Zetrix shares fell 18.75% or 1.5 sen to 6.5 sen today, giving it a market capitalisation of RM496 million. The stock has fallen 92% year to date.
05e59375db2409ee: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged parents to take greater responsibility for monitoring their children’s activities and upbringing, warning that a lack of supervision could jeopardise their future.

Speaking to reporters after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Al-Muqarrabin here, Anwar said parents should pay closer attention to their children’s daily routines, including their studies, whereabouts and whether they were at risk of getting involved with drugs.
“Parents sometimes do not even know whether their children are reading books, whether they are coming home at night, whether they are doing their homework or getting involved with drugs,” he said.
Anwar said cooperation between parents and families was important in addressing issues affecting children, including mental health problems and autism.
He said the Cabinet had discussed several such issues earlier today, which required collective efforts to find solutions.
“Besides the calls I hear every day for the government to take action, I want to take this opportunity to urge parents to take responsibility,” he said.
Anwar also expressed concern that some parents might leave their children to their circumstances without providing proper supervision, guidance and education.
“I worry about their upbringing and future if parents simply surrender to the circumstances without supervising and educating them,” he said.
5670525ead317715: BENGALURU: Novak Djokovic missed a big chance to strengthen his push for a place at the end-of-year ATP Finals after a loss to Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel, leaving the Serb with precious few opportunities to make up ground in the race to Turin.
Back in Basel for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old Djokovic fell 6-7(4) ,7-5 7-6(5) , in the second round on Thursday, his first defeat by German veteran Struff in nine meetings.
"I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So I was very happy," said Struff, who clinched the win with his 27th ace of the match.

"The last serve went into the corner like many balls today. I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. The last eight times, he beat me very easily. So I'm very pleased with the performance."

The result left Djokovic 11th in the qualification race for the eight-player season finale, 319 points behind ninth-placed Rafael Jodar, who currently occupies the final qualifying spot with the injured Jannik Sinner not playing in Turin.

Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton all have places in the ATP Finals starting on Nov 15, leaving Djokovic battling for one of the remaining spots with next week's Paris Masters offering him another opportunity to pick up points.

Djokovic will head to the Nov 2-8 Paris Masters as a record seven-times champion, but has not said whether he would consider entering the ATP 250 event in Stockholm afterwards if he still needs points to secure a finals' place.
He missed the previous two editions of the ATP Finals due to injury but had indicated that he intended to return to the event he has won a record seven times if he qualifies.
The 24-times Grand Slam champion has endured another tough season physically, though his run to the Australian Open final, a Wimbledon semi-final and his Beijing triumph have provided notable highs.
Few will write off Djokovic's chances of reaching Turin even at this stage, given the resilience that he has shown throughout his glittering career.
"I won the title in Beijing a few weeks ago, which was definitely my best week this year apart from the Grand Slam final in Australia," Djokovic told reporters before the tournament in Basel.

"It's been a year with a lot of struggles, particularly physically, but I'm still here and as competitive as anybody. If somebody beats me, well done, good job, but I'm definitely going to fight and not give these youngsters too easy a stroll on court. They have to earn their victories.
"That's also what motivates me: seeing how I can match up with players 15-plus years younger than me. It's been quite an interesting process to experience."
e6672ad39293d594: Home secretary’s colleagues fear homelessness will rise as a result of changes to the asylum system Shabana Mahmood has infuriated ministerial colleagues by failing to share what they see as crucial information about the impact of her migration changes. Sources say the home secretary has repeatedly refused to reveal how much she expects homelessness to rise as a result of changes to the asylum system. Continue reading...
b50eb5fa245fc2cd: Up to 1.4 million people could benefit from change to trading allowance announced in budget, with some saving hundreds in tax The amount Britons can earn from a side hustle without paying tax will rise to £3,000 next year in a fillip for those who make extra cash from hobbies or reselling. Up to 1.4 million people could benefit from the change announced in the budget, with the chancellor confirming the tax-free “trading” allowance will increase from £1,000 to £3,000 in April 2027. Continue reading...
68c414d7023cd1a8: LABUAN: Defence minister Khaled Nordin received the first FA-50M light combat aircraft acquired by the air force today, marking an important milestone in Malaysia's efforts to strengthen its air defence capabilities.
The aircraft, developed by Korea Aerospace Industries, was flown from Sacheon to the air force's base here.
"The official handover ceremony is scheduled to take place in mid-November at the Kuantan air base," Khaled told reporters at the Labuan base.

Describing the acquisition as a significant moment for the country in enhancing its military capabilities and safeguarding national sovereignty, he said the acquisition also supported the air force's long-term capability development under its Capability Development Plan 2055.

He said the government would also consider acquiring a second batch of more modern and advanced fighter aircraft to further strengthen Malaysia's air defence capabilities, although the country of origin for future procurement has yet to be determined.

"The 18 FA-50M aircraft were procured under Malaysia's Fighter Lead-In Training and Light Combat Aircraft programme, following the planned decommissioning of the air force's Hawk aircraft in 2028," he said.
Khaled said the air force was expected to receive six FA-50M aircraft by April 2027, with the remaining units scheduled for delivery in early 2028.
He said the ministry would determine the number of FA-50M aircraft to be based in Labuan following the decommissioning of the Hawk aircraft.
The FA-50M is a two-seat aircraft capable of supporting crewed flight training as well as demanding operational missions.
It can reach speeds of up to Mach 1.2, enabling it to fly faster than the speed of sound and operate at high altitudes.
Fifty-seven core personnel comprising six pilots, six engineering officers and 45 technicians have completed their training in South Korea to spearhead the new squadron.
All six pilots in the initial training group completed their flight training programme on Oct 21.
Khaled said the aircraft would be operated by No 15 Squadron, which already has more than 200 personnel, with preparations for their home base in Kuantan.
91fe72e2cc8b5938: ATLANTA: US state secretary Marco Rubio will host his G20 counterparts, including Russia's Sergei Lavrov, for talks on Friday that are expected to be fractious, with wars in Ukraine and Iran and surging energy prices fanning discord.

The foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, taking place just days before crucial US midterm elections, will set the stage for a December G20 leaders' summit in Miami at pesident Donald Trump's Doral resort.

Few breakthroughs are expected this week from the Group of 20 economies - which include China, India, Russia, Japan, Germany and France - as officials face divisions over Moscow's war on Ukraine and fallout from conflict with Iran.
Russia has been shunned by most of the West after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and Lavrov himself remains under international sanctions.

Rubio's encounter with Lavrov - whose presence adds an additional layer of tension - will be closely watched as Washington pursues diplomacy on Ukraine while seeking Moscow's cooperation on reining in fuel prices, a key campaign issue in the midterms.
"The G20 is no longer really a forum where foreign ministers can reach agreement on a statement," a diplomatic source said.

The source added that the US G20 presidency intends for Miami's summit to serve "more as a demonstration of American power - and of US commitments to growth, deregulation, trade and business - rather than as a summit with grand ambitions on substantive issues".
Instead of a final declaration, the source expects a chair summary drafted by the US to be published from this week's meeting.
The Trump administration, which is set to hand the rotating G20 leadership to Britain, sees the platform as having strayed from its core mission.
Washington has pledged to return the grouping to its goal of driving economic growth, arguing that security and economic prosperity are "inextricably linked".

"Conversations in Atlanta will provide an opportunity to discuss energy and supply chain challenges as well as identify ways to collectively address the impact of geopolitical tensions on economic security," a US state department official said.

They stressed the importance of energy access - necessary for tech like artificial intelligence - and flagged a "shared resolve to confront urgent crises and keep critical sea lanes open to commerce without threats or tolls".
'Test case'
Global energy prices have rocketed since US-Israel strikes on Iran from late February triggered Tehran's blockage of the Strait of Hormuz.

"This is the last test case the G20 has, at least under the US G20 presidency, until Miami," Alisha Chhangani of the Atlantic Council told AFP. Its outcomes will affect how the December summit shapes up.
She expects Washington will seek to argue that security shocks are also economic shocks.
"It will likely push for agreement on what 'freedom of navigation' means within and beyond Hormuz, a crucial waterway for oil and gas transit," she said.
However, this could face objections from China, which dissented against wording on free navigation in Hormuz and worldwide at an earlier gathering of finance ministers.
"China's top diplomat Wang Yi will not be in Atlanta, and is instead sending his deputy," the US state department said.
Meanwhile, the possibility of further escalation in the Middle East is mounting, with Israel threatening to strike Iran and Trump signalling he could attack after Tuesday's midterm elections.
Lavrov attendance
In Atlanta, Rubio is also due to cross paths with Lavrov, who has already reached Atlanta according to Russian state media.
It comes ahead of fresh negotiations between Moscow, Kyiv and Washington in November.
"The appearance of Lavrov, who plans to argue against international sanctions at the gathering, will likely frustrate European ministers," Chhangani said.

It is not surprising, however, as Washington has welcomed Russian officials to this year's G20 events - while excluding member South Africa - and Trump has invited his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to Miami in December.
Trump has eased some sanctions on Moscow recently while touting a deal for Russia to sell diesel as prices soared, squeezing Americans.
The diplomatic source stressed that Russia's G20 presence "in no way legitimises its actions".

All eyes will also be on US engagement with Brazil, whose foreign minister will be in attendance, after Washington granted entry to Flavio Bolsonaro following his defeat in Sunday's presidential election.
0c96fe0fcb37183b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with Bersatu follows a mechanism previously agreed upon under the Perikatan Nasional-Barisan Nasional (PN-BN) government when he was Opposition Leader.
He said the arrangement was based on an understanding reached with the administration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, when Anwar was leading the Opposition.
“That was the understanding in principle, similar to what I did as Opposition Leader with the government at the time, when the government comprised Umno, PAS and Bersatu.

“So, when they discussed and proposed the allocations, that was what was implemented. There is nothing unusual about it,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Al-Muqarrabin, Bandar Tasik Selatan here.

Anwar said the current arrangement was also based on a similar understanding, stressing that parliamentary allocations had continued as usual for both government and Opposition MPs despite criticism that the government was withholding funds.
He said the mechanism was not introduced by his administration but followed the approach used by the previous government, which included Bersatu, PAS and Barisan Nasional.

“Allocations through MPs are bound by an understanding, just as was done by the Perikatan Nasional and Barisan Nasional governments when they were in power and which we signed. At that time, I was the Opposition Leader and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri was the prime minister,” he said.
Anwar described Bersatu’s agreement to the arrangement as a positive development, adding that other parties were also free to participate if they agreed to the same mechanism.
He said the allocations would be based on the current Budget and could be channelled by the end of this year after it had been debated and approved.
“Once the Budget has been debated and approved, we can channel the allocations by the end of this year in accordance with the understanding reached,” he said.
Anwar also said there were no conditions imposed on Opposition MPs under the arrangement.
“There are no conditions imposed on any Opposition MP. There are no conditions,” he said.

Bersatu signed the CSA with the government yesterday, with party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin saying its MPs would receive the same constituency development allocations as government backbenchers.
In return, the seven Opposition MPs involved in the agreement pledged support for Anwar’s administration until the end of the parliamentary term, as well as the Supply Bill 2027.
Muhyiddin had also stressed that Bersatu would remain in the Opposition and continue to perform its role of providing checks and balances.
c6fecb81bbfbcb87: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has ordered the consultant and developer of the condominium project linked to the Paya Terubong landslide to prepare a site inspection report and outline mitigation measures.
Local government, town and country planning committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the inspection report should include maps of the risky slope areas and mitigation plans.
The developer has also been ordered to amend its erosion and sediment control plan based on the site's present condition and undertake temporary stabilisation measures.
"MBPP has also ordered the developer and consultant to control surface water flow by diverting runoff from the top of the slope.

"This will be done by setting up temporary drainage, inspecting existing drainage for overflows or leaks, and covering exposed slopes with geotextiles or appropriate temporary protection," H'ng said at a press conference at the state assembly building today.
MBPP mayor A Rajendran said the occupational safety and health department (DOSH) has been carrying out a site investigation since Oct 26 to determine the cause of the landslide.
"They will summon all involved parties to ascertain what actually transpired at the site, followed by legal action should there be any negligence or failure by any party," he said.
The council issued a stop-work order for the project, which includes the construction of a road, following the landslide on Sunday which killed a 73-year-old doctor at a house in Taman Sri Rambai.
SAM calls for state commission of inquiry
At another press conference earlier, Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM) urged the Penang government to establish a state commission of inquiry to investigate the landslide.
A similar commission had been established to investigate the Granito landslide that claimed 11 lives in Tanjung Bungah in 2017.
SAM president Meenakshi Raman said this commission was needed to determine the root cause of the landslide and if there were elements of negligence.
The commission would also outline measures that need to be taken to prevent similar tragedies from happening in future, she said.
Soil scientist and environmentalist Kam Suan Pheng of Penang Hills Watch said repeated slope cementing works were done on the area near the affected row of houses from 2018 to this year.
This indicates that the slope was already unstable, she said.
Rajendran said the project was approved after several assessments conducted by consultants as well as MBPP, DOSH, and the mineral and geoscience department.
He said the slope stabilisation works were required, as per the approvals given to the project's consultant and developer.
Separately, H'ng dismissed SAM's call for a state commission of inquiry, saying the state government wants to wait for DOSH's investigations to be completed first.
e0e7fcc545d0c359: PETALING JAYA: Mahkamah Tinggi Shah Alam memerintahkan MajuBina Resources Sdn Bhd membayar RM15.32 juta kepada Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) kerana gagal menyiapkan projek Jalinan Digital Negara (Jendela) 1 di Sabah mengikut jadual.
SKMM berkata, tindakan undang-undang itu difailkannya pada Februari lalu bagi menuntut bayaran ganti rugi susulan kelewatan projek di bawah inisiatif Pemberian Perkhidmatan Sejagat (USP).
Mahkamah turut memerintahkan syarikat terbabit membayar kos sebanyak RM5,000 kepada SKMM.
Menurut SKMM, setiap projek infrastruktur komunikasi yang dibiayai dana USP mesti dilaksanakan mengikut obligasi kontrak dan tempoh dipersetujui.

"Pematuhan terhadap ketetapan ini penting bagi memastikan pelaksanaan projek berjalan lancar serta manfaat ketersambungan digital dapat dinikmati rakyat, khususnya di kawasan luar bandar dan kurang mendapat liputan," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Katanya, keputusan mahkamah menyerlahkan kepentingan akauntabiliti dalam pelaksanaan projek infrastruktur komunikasi negara.
“SKMM akan terus memastikan dana USP dimanfaatkan secara bertanggungjawab untuk meningkatkan akses rakyat kepada perkhidmatan komunikasi berkualiti,” katanya.
Inisiatif projek Jendera 1 bertujuan memperluas liputan dan akses kepada perkhidmatan komunikasi, khususnya di kawasan luar bandar dan kurang mendapat liputan.
53b4f13509574b04: RIYADH: Yemen's Houthis denied launching any attack towards Saudi Arabia on Friday, after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by the group over the Mecca region.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree dismissed the coalition's account as false in a post on X, saying the group had not carried out any operation towards Saudi territory.
He said its operations target Saudi oil facilities and military bases.
The Iran-aligned Houthis have launched a series of cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia targeting military installations, airports and energy infrastructure.
The group has repeatedly denied targeting Mecca and Medina, Islam's two holiest cities, rejecting previous Saudi-led coalition accusations that it had launched drones towards the cities.
1a7bab84f359b032: In today’s newsletter: Benjamin Netanyahu has been left without a majority, now it is up to the coalition to find out whether the desire for change will prove to be a defining political moment Good morning. It was described by many Israelis as the most consequential election in their country’s history. 6a71b2e5d2a70e69: Welcome to another instalment of On Call, the reader-contributed column The Register publishes each Friday as a cathartic service for readers who know that dealing with tech support BS can be a cow of a job.
This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Jason" who told us he had helped an agricultural equipment dealer with his computer issues for about 20 years.

"One day this guy called me to ask if I could help at a farm in Yorkshire, where he'd arranged the supply and installation of a fairly substantial system that used a computer to do effectively everything for a few hundred cattle," he told On Call.
"That meant individually feeding them, measuring milk yields, planning pregnancies, and periodically submitting all the data to the government."
Jason said other tech support folk had tried, and failed, to fix the system.
"This had somewhat soured the relationship between the agricultural equipment dealer and the farmer," he punned in his email to On Call.
Well punned, Jason.
But we digress.

"Despite not being fond of wading around in cow shit at four in the morning, I agreed to take a look at the system," Jason told us. By this time he had learned that the farm produced many tons of milk each week, so assumed he would find serious industrial-scale tech once he reached the farm.
That assumption was wrong.

"When I arrived, the first thing that I found to worry about was that the whole thing was controlled by proprietary software on a single PC running Windows XP – just after Microsoft ended mainstream support."
The other things to worry about were all acts of omission: the farm had no backups, no spare PC, and nobody on site to maintain the PC.

Jason asked if anyone was responsible for keeping the computer up to date with the security patches and was told the farmer's 14-year-old grandson had done some computer studies at school, so he got the job.
That lad had either not discovered, or deleted, the many rather racy videos Jason found on the PC.
"When the farmer's wife learned of this, there was what can best be described as a hullabaloo," Jason told On Call.

As he dug into the mess, Jason found that the computer was sending milk production data to Her Majesty's Government. He also found that neither the government, nor the farm management software vendor, had bothered to require installation of a firewall.
Jason says he installed one, made a few other tweaks, and got the system working.
"Everyone seemed pleased, or at least they did until they got my bill," he wrote. "And to be fair, they did pay it promptly."
Jason never heard from the farm again.
"I don't know if that's because it's still working OK, or if they're just too embarrassed to see me again, or they found someone cheaper who could cope with my recommendations," he wrote.

What's the strangest or dirtiest place you've been asked to deliver tech support? Don't cheese us off by holding back! Click here to send us your story so we can milk it for all it's worth in a future instalment of On Call. ®
5cda5184ad58384c: SINGAPORE: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated US$6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever.
Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about US$3 billion located so far.
It gave no update on the status of the remaining US$3.3 billion.
The possible hacking sent crypto prices lower. Bitcoin hit a six-week low and was last down 3% at US$76,469.82, while Ether was down more than 3% at US$2,185.83.
Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of Bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading.
Here are some comments from analysts and investors:
Eric Jardine, head of research at Chainalysis, said the investigation into the hack was ongoing and that the cause had yet to be confirmed.
"The investigation is ongoing, and we cannot yet confirm the cause of the hack.
"As of 8.30pm, we have confirmed that at least US$5.912 billion was stolen, with funds moving across multiple blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Ripple and several Layer 2 networks.
"Binance has also confirmed that approximately US$3 billion has been frozen.
"Blockchain transparency and coordination across the industry are helping disrupt the movement of stolen funds.
"Our investigators are actively identifying additional opportunities to freeze funds and support recovery efforts," he said.

Meanwhile, Amanda He, CIO at ChainUp Investment in Singapore, said the initial market decline may have been triggered by the hacker selling the coins, with panic spreading further as the Asian trading session got underway.
"The initial drop may have been because the hacker was selling the coins.

However, after 8am, as the Asian morning session got underway, that has caused panic sentiment to spread further... Binance is still the largest exchange in the market by trading volume, so it is really at the centre of this storm — and at the centre of market activity.
"We don't have a large position on Binance. It accounts for less than 20% of our overall holdings.

"But for the positions we do have there, we've sold everything for now. Anything that can be moved out, we move first. Things that can't be moved, we sell, shifting into safe-haven assets instead such as stablecoins. Withdrawals have now been suspended," she said.
Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group in Hong Kong, said the implications of the incident could extend beyond the immediate loss of assets.

"We believe the implications of the Binance incident could well extend beyond the immediate loss of assets. The incident could rank among the largest security breaches in the history of the cryptocurrency industry.

"Our bigger concern is the potential liquidity impact. As the largest digital-asset trading platform globally, any disruption to Binance's deposit and withdrawal operations could affect market makers' ability to move capital across venues," Sun said.
Geoffrey Kendrick, head of digital assets research at Standard Chartered in London, said cryptocurrency prices could face further declines.
"I suspect the negative price action still has some way to go. Only after assets are unfrozen and more detail of the hack emerges will we find a new base," he said.
Damon Xu, founder of 1Token in Singapore, said the incident could prompt investors to scale back cross-exchange strategies and reduce leverage.
"We expect cross-exchange strategies to be scaled back and leverage to decline.

"Even if affected users are ultimately made whole, funds being locked during the interim could leave traders in a situation where they are profitable on one venue but unable to access capital, while facing margin shortages and forced liquidations on another.
"Decentralised exchanges could stand to benefit. The strong performance of Hyperliquid during this period is noteworthy, as some capital and trading activity may migrate on-chain," Xu added.
Aravind Srinivasan, head of systematic OTC business at crypto market maker GSR, described the incident as the biggest hack in history and said market liquidity had weakened.
"It's the biggest hack in history... spreads are wider and liquidity is thin in Binance too on spot.
"The average bid/ask spread on spot Bitcoin was five times wider than normal earlier this morning, and 2.5 times for Ether. Spreads have since narrowed slightly," he added.
Kenneth Goh, director of private wealth management at UOB Kay Hian in Singapore, said the incident could prompt investors to reassess the security of cryptocurrency exchanges.
"Crypto has a long record of exchange thefts. Mt Gox collapsed in 2014 after losing close to US$500 million in Bitcoin, and Bybit lost about US$1.5 billion only last year.
"What stands out this time is where it happened. The world's largest exchange should have the strongest controls in the industry, and it has still been breached.
"Investors will now look more closely at where their assets are held and who is responsible when something goes wrong," Goh said.
Mark Karpeles, CEO of Karpeles Lab and former head of Mt Gox, said Binance appeared to have distributed its assets across multiple systems to limit the impact of a hack.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems (ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets), but even so a single hack is a large loss.
"It looks like the attacker somehow managed to get a valid delegation for both Binance 14 and Binance 16, which means they likely found the private key used by those addresses," he said.
Yuya Hasegawa, market analyst at cryptocurrency exchange Bitbank in Tokyo, said the reported scale of the incident was alarming, although the full extent of the damage remained unclear.

"The reported scale of the incident is certainly alarming. However, the full extent of the damage remains unclear, particularly as stablecoin issuers have already frozen a substantial portion of the affected assets.

"The biggest concern is not necessarily the amount stolen itself, but whether the incident triggers a broader loss of confidence in centralised exchanges, potentially leading to further withdrawals, liquidity disruptions, and forced selling.

"That said, if Binance can demonstrate that customer assets remain secure, cover any losses, and restore normal operations promptly, the market impact could prove relatively short-lived. Bitcoin's underlying fundamentals have not been directly compromised by this incident," Hasegawa said.
Jeff Ko, chief analyst at ViaBTC in Hong Kong, said he did not expect the stolen bitcoin to add significant selling pressure, although he warned that Ether could face continued selling pressure.
"I don't expect the stolen BTC to add much selling pressure. Bitcoin addresses can't be frozen, but every coin is traceable on-chain, and Bitcoin has no mixing tool as deep or liquid as Tornado Cash.

"In effect, much of that BTC is likely to stay 'locked' and might take years to go to the market. ETH is a different story. It can be laundered far more easily through Tornado Cash, so I would expect ongoing selling pressure and relative weakness in ETH. For perspective, after the Bybit hack, markets took only weeks to recover.

"Beyond sentiment, this incident once again highlights the security risks of centralised exchanges, and of the crypto market more broadly amid AI development. That said, the breach appears to stem from how transactions were signed and authorised, not from a smart contract exploit," he said.
Joshua Chu, co-chair of the Hong Kong Web3 Association, said the incident had implications for regulators, law enforcement, the legal system and cryptocurrency industry participants.

"This incident puts four fronts in play: regulators protecting the public, law enforcement pursuing offenders, civil litigation recovering assets, and ecosystem players ensuring they do not become the getaway route for stolen funds.

"For crypto players still resisting government cooperation, the contradiction is awkward: regulation is ‘overreach’ while profits flow, but government is ‘not doing enough’ when the money disappears," Chu said.
96cd52eaceb76e1b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Malaysia Airlines has advised passengers travelling from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) between October 30 and November 1 to allow extra time to reach the airport due to expected traffic congestion during the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia 2026.

In a statement posted on social media today, the airline said heavy traffic and road delays were expected in surrounding areas and on highways leading to KLIA during the MotoGP event, which is being held at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit.
